passages.en: And if the <hi rend="spaced">sheriff</hi> <seg type="recension">(that is, the reeve <hi rend="spaced">of the town or vill</hi>)</seg> is accused that <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">the counterfeiter</hi>)</seg> did <hi rend="spaced">what he did</hi> by his licence, let him clear himself with threefold purgation, <hi rend="bold">of oath or of hot iron </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(that is, ordeal)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold">,</hi> which the English <hi rend="spaced">name</hi> <hi rend="italic">thrifealde lade</hi> [threefold exculpation] <seg type="recension">(with a purgation which the E. <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">þrefeald l.</hi>, <hi rend="bold">of o. or of h. i.,</hi> which the E. <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">ordel</hi>)</hi></seg><hi rend="bold">;</hi> and if he fails in the purgation, let him suffer what the <hi rend="spaced">false moneyer</hi> suffered.

passages.text: Mensurę et pondera <hi rend="spaced">per totum</hi> regnum <hi rend="spaced">Anglię</hi> ita corrigantur, ut sint recta<ptr n="15" target="IICn_9.lnote.oe.15"/> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="bold">unita</hi>)</seg>.<ptr n="16" target="IICn_9.lnote.oe.16-2"/>

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">über</hi> r. <hi rend="italic">schreibt</hi> u. <hi rend="italic">H; nur</hi> u. <hi rend="italic">Lb S; nur</hi> r. <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: H writes u. above r.; only u. Lb S; only r. Cb

passages.en: Measures and weights <hi rend="spaced">throughout the whole</hi> kingdom <hi rend="spaced">of England</hi> shall be so corrected that they be right <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="bold">uniform</hi>)</seg>.

passages.text: Hę<ptr n="1" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.1"/> sunt consuetudines<ptr n="2" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.2-2"/> <hi rend="spaced">regis</hi>, quas<ptr n="3" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.3-2"/> habet super<ptr n="4" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.4-4"/> omnes homines in Westsexe<ptr n="5" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.5-4"/>: forisfacturam, <hi rend="spaced">quam Angli uocant</hi> mundbrece<ptr n="6" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.6-4"/>, hamsocne<ptr n="7" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.7-3"/>, <hi rend="spaced">hoc</hi><ptr n="8" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.8-4"/> est inuasio in <hi rend="spaced">propria domo aut infra curiam</hi> causa<ptr n="9" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.9-2"/> <hi rend="spaced">alicuius mali</hi>, foresteal<ptr n="10" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.10-2"/>, <hi rend="spaced">quod nos possumus dicere contrastationem</hi><ptr n="11" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.11-2"/>, <hi rend="spaced">causa mali</hi>; ferdƿite<ptr n="12" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.12-2"/>, <hi rend="spaced">quod nos possumus dicere dimissionem belli</hi>; hę sunt<ptr n="13" target="IICn_12.lnote.oe.13-2"/>, <hi rend="spaced">inquam</hi>, consuetudines regis, nisi rex uelit aliquem <hi rend="spaced">honorare</hi>, dando ei <hi rend="spaced">quod sui iuris est</hi>.

notes.de: su. o. ho., quas ha. in <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: su. o. ho., quas ha. in Cb

notes.de: in W. s. o. ho. <hi rend="italic">Lb S Pl Ct</hi>
notes.en: in W. s. o. ho. Lb S Pl Ct

notes.de: hans. <hi rend="italic">Cb;</hi> homs. <hi rend="italic">Lb S Ct;</hi> -soke <hi rend="italic">Pl</hi>
notes.en: hans. Cb; homs. Lb S Ct; -soke Pl

passages.en: These are the rights of the <hi rend="spaced">king</hi> which he has over all men in Wessex: the forfeiture <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">mundbrece</hi> [breach of protection], <hi rend="italic">hamsocne</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">that</hi> is, attack <hi rend="spaced">in one's own house or within the courtyard</hi> for the sake <hi rend="spaced">of some evil</hi>, <hi rend="italic">foresteal</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which we can call 'obstruction'</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">for the sake of evil</hi>; <hi rend="italic">ferdƿite</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which we can call 'desertion of the army'</hi>; these are, <hi rend="spaced">I say</hi>, the king's rights, unless the king wishes to <hi rend="spaced">honour</hi> someone by giving him <hi rend="spaced">what is of his right</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis <hi rend="spaced">fecerit</hi> opus expulsi, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi> útlages ƿeorc<ptr n="14" target="IICn_13.lnote.oe.14"/>, uideat rex de pace.
passages.en: If anyone <hi rend="spaced">does</hi> the work of an outlaw, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">útlages ƿeorc</hi>, let the king see to [his] peace.

passages.text: Uerum si ipse habet alodium <seg type="recension">(bocland<ptr n="15" target="IICn_13-1.lnote.oe.15"/>)</seg>, <seg type="recension">(suum<ptr n="16" target="IICn_13-1.lnote.oe.16-2"/>)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">totum</hi> sit regis, cuiuscumque homo<ptr n="17" target="IICn_13-1.lnote.oe.17-2"/> sit.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">gleichzeitig übergeschr. nur H; fehlt übr.</hi>
notes.en: written above by a contemporary hand, only H; lacking in the others

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">aus Cb; fehlt H Lb S</hi>
notes.en: from Cb; lacking in H Lb S

passages.en: But if he has allodial land <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="italic">bocland</hi>)</seg>, let <seg type="recension">(his)</seg> <hi rend="spaced">whole</hi> be the king's, whosesoever man he be.

passages.text: Et qui exulem <seg type="recension">(quem<ptr n="18" target="IICn_13-2.lnote.oe.18"/> Angli <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> <hi rend="bold">utlaga</hi>)</seg> pauerit post ex<hi rend="spaced">pulsionem, quod Angli dicunt</hi><ptr n="19" target="IICn_13-2.lnote.oe.19-2"/> fede oþþe fermie<ptr n="20" target="IICn_13-2.lnote.oe.20-2"/>, det regi <hi rend="spaced">centum solidos</hi>, nisi se purgauerit, quod illum nescisset expulsum <hi rend="bold">clamatum</hi><ptr n="1" target="IICn_13-2.lnote.oe.1"/><hi rend="bold">, quod Angli dicunt gecydne</hi><ptr n="2" target="IICn_13-2.lnote.oe.2-2"/><hi rend="bold"> utlage.</hi><ptr n="3" target="IICn_13-2.lnote.oe.3"/>

notes.de: q. A. u. u. <hi rend="italic">fehlt Cb</hi>
notes.en: q. A. u. u. lacking in Cb

notes.de: uocant <hi rend="italic">Lb S; am Rande</hi> <hi rend="spaced">flemeneferme</hi> <hi rend="italic">S</hi>
notes.en: uocant Lb S; in the margin <hi rend="italic">flemeneferme</hi> S

notes.de: oðe forðie <hi rend="italic">Cb;</hi> en ferme <hi rend="italic">Lb S</hi>
notes.en: oðe forðie Cb; en ferme Lb S

passages.en: And whoever has fed an exile <seg type="recension">(whom the English <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">utlaga</hi></hi>)</seg> after the ex<hi rend="spaced">pulsion, which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">fede oþþe fermie</hi> [feeds or harbours], let him give the king <hi rend="spaced">a hundred shillings</hi>, unless he clears himself [by oath] that he did not know him [to be] expelled <hi rend="bold">[and] proclaimed, which the English call <hi rend="italic">gecydne utlage</hi> [declared outlaw].</hi>

passages.text: In lege Mercia rex habet easdem <hi rend="spaced">consuetudines</hi>.
passages.en: In the Mercian law the king has the same <hi rend="spaced">rights</hi>.

passages.text: In<ptr n="4" target="IICn_15.lnote.oe.4-2"/> lege autem<ptr n="5" target="IICn_15.lnote.oe.5-2"/> Danorum habet<ptr n="6" target="IICn_15.lnote.oe.6-3"/> rex has <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">consuetudines</hi><ptr n="7" target="IICn_15.lnote.oe.7-3"/>)</seg>: uiolationem <hi rend="bold">monetę,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi> <hi rend="bold">feohƿíte,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">dimissionem belli</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli</hi><ptr n="8" target="IICn_15.lnote.oe.8-3"/><hi rend="spaced"> dicunt</hi> ferdƿite, fractionem pacis, <hi rend="spaced">quod dicunt</hi> griðbrece<ptr n="9" target="IICn_15.lnote.oe.9-3"/>, inuasionem<ptr n="10" target="IICn_15.lnote.oe.10"/> in domo uel in <hi rend="spaced">curia, quod dicunt hamsocne</hi>, nisi <hi rend="spaced">rex uelit</hi><ptr n="11" target="IICn_15.lnote.oe.11"/> <hi rend="spaced">dare quod suum est</hi>.

notes.de: Secundum legem D. — cons. <hi rend="italic">roth Cb</hi>
notes.en: Secundum legem D. — cons. in red Cb
only Cb; lacking in the others
altered late to -che Cb; gritbreche Lb

passages.en: But in the law of the Danes the king has these <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">rights</hi>)</seg>: violation <hi rend="bold">of the coinage,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">feohƿíte</hi>,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">desertion of the army</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">ferdƿite</hi>, breach of the peace, <hi rend="spaced">which they call</hi> <hi rend="italic">griðbrece</hi>, attack in a house or in a <hi rend="spaced">courtyard, which they call <hi rend="italic">hamsocne</hi></hi>, unless <hi rend="spaced">the king wishes</hi> <hi rend="spaced">to give what is his</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis iniustas leges adinuerit<ptr n="18" target="IICn_15-1.lnote.oe.18-3"/> et iudicauerit, aut causa odii aut<ptr n="19" target="IICn_15-1.lnote.oe.19-3"/> adquisitionis pecunię, sit reus regi <hi rend="bold">XL</hi><ptr n="20" target="IICn_15-1.lnote.oe.20-3"/> sol. in lege Anglorum, nisi<ptr n="21" target="IICn_15-1.lnote.oe.21-2"/> iuramento affirmauerit, se rectius<ptr n="22" target="IICn_15-1.lnote.oe.22-2"/> <hi rend="spaced">iudicare</hi> nescisse, et postea careat <hi rend="spaced">liberalitate</hi><ptr n="23" target="IICn_15-1.lnote.oe.23-2"/> sua, nisi eam á rege<ptr n="24" target="IICn_15-1.lnote.oe.24-2"/> redimat ad <hi rend="spaced">uelle regis</hi>.
passages.en: If anyone devises unjust laws and judges [by them], either for the sake of hatred or of acquiring money, let him be liable to the king for <hi rend="bold">40</hi> shillings in the law of the English, unless he affirms by oath that he did not know how <hi rend="spaced">to judge</hi> more rightly, and afterwards let him lose his <hi rend="spaced">noble rank</hi>, unless he redeem it from the king at <hi rend="spaced">the king's will</hi>.

passages.text: In lege Danorum erit reus forisfacturę, <hi rend="spaced">quam</hi> <hi rend="bold">Dani</hi> <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> lahslit . . .<ptr n="*" target="IICn_15-1a.lnote.oe.star"/>

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">folgen vier Zeilen, vielleicht aus Northu. Priestergesetz</hi> 51 <hi rend="italic">ff., wo vgl.</hi>
notes.en: four lines follow, perhaps from Northu. Priests’ Law 51 ff.; cf. there

passages.en: In the law of the Danes he shall be liable for the forfeiture <hi rend="spaced">which</hi> <hi rend="bold">the Danes</hi> <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">lahslit</hi> [fine for breach of law] . . .

passages.text: In lege eorum<ptr n="e" target="InCn_II-15-1b.lnote.oe.e"/> liberalis hominis lahslit uocant X dimidię marcę, hoc est V marcę<ptr n="f" target="InCn_II-15-1b.lnote.oe.f"/>; hominis alodium<ptr n="6" target="InCn_II-15-1b.lnote.oe.6"/> <seg type="recension">(bocland<ptr n="7" target="InCn_II-15-1b.lnote.oe.7"/>)</seg> habentis sex dimidię marcę, hoc est tres marcę; uillani lahslit, quem<ptr n="8" target="InCn_II-15-1b.lnote.oe.8"/> Angli uocant ceorlman<ptr n="9" target="InCn_II-15-1b.lnote.oe.9"/> XII orę<ptr n="10" target="InCn_II-15-1b.lnote.oe.10"/>.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">nämlich</hi> Danorum. <hi rend="italic">Diese Busssätze zahlen bezw.</hi> cyninges þegn [liberalis <hi rend="italic">setzen Inst. oft für</hi> þegn], landagende, cyrlisc man <hi rend="italic">nach</hi> Northu. 51 <hi rend="italic">ff., o. S.</hi> 383, <hi rend="italic">deren Benutzung hierfür auch Steenstrup</hi> Danelag 267 <hi rend="italic">annimmt</hi>
notes.en: namely Danorum. These rates of compensation are paid respectively by the cyninges þegn [the Inst. often put liberalis for þegn], the landagende and the cyrlisc man according to Northu. 51 ff., above p. 383, which Steenstrup Danelag 267 also assumes to have been used here
in the 12th cent. 1 mark = ⅔ pound
only H, written above, missing in the rest

passages.en: In their law they call the <hi rend="italic">lahslit</hi> [fine for breach of law] of a free man of rank (thegn) ten half-marks, that is five marks; of a man having allodial land <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="italic">bocland</hi>)</seg> six half-marks, that is three marks; the <hi rend="italic">lahslit</hi> of a villein, whom the English call <hi rend="italic">ceorlman</hi>, twelve ores.

passages.text: Qui expulsum pauerit aut <hi rend="spaced">detinuerit pacifice</hi>, quem<ptr n="12" target="IICn_15a.lnote.oe.12-2"/> Angli <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi><ptr n="13" target="IICn_15a.lnote.oe.13"/> friðleasne<ptr n="14" target="IICn_15a.lnote.oe.14"/> man, reddat regi, sicut lex est, <hi rend="spaced">plenam emendationem</hi>, <hi rend="bold">et illi</hi><ptr n="15" target="IICn_15a.lnote.oe.15"/><hi rend="bold"> qui</hi><ptr n="16" target="IICn_15a.lnote.oe.16"/><hi rend="bold"> expulsum expulit despectum suum, si ita iustum</hi><ptr n="17" target="IICn_15a.lnote.oe.17"/><hi rend="bold"> est.</hi>

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">auf Rasur H;</hi> quod <hi rend="italic">Lb; verb. aus</hi> quod <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: on an erasure H; quod Lb; corrected from quod Cb

notes.de: expulsionem illi et qui <hi rend="italic">wiederholt Cb</hi>
notes.en: expulsionem illi et qui repeated by Cb

passages.en: Whoever feeds an expelled man or <hi rend="spaced">keeps [him] peaceably</hi>, whom the English <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">friðleasne man</hi> [man without peace], let him pay the king, as the law is, <hi rend="spaced">full compensation</hi>, <hi rend="bold">and to him who expelled the expelled man his contempt-fine, if that is just.</hi>

passages.text: Qui rectum iudicium et iustam legem abnegat, sit forisfactus<ptr n="1" target="IICn_15-2.lnote.oe.1-6"/> ei cui <hi rend="spaced">iustum est</hi>: si regi, det<ptr n="2" target="IICn_15-2.lnote.oe.2-6"/> illi <hi rend="bold">XL</hi><ptr n="†" target="IICn_15-2.lnote.oe.dagger-2"/> solidos, si comiti <hi rend="bold">XX</hi> solidos, si hundredo <hi rend="bold">X</hi> solidos, si contra omnes hos<ptr n="3" target="IICn_15-2.lnote.oe.3-5"/>, <hi rend="spaced">omnibus reddat</hi>.

notes.en: det i. lacking in Lb S

passages.en: Whoever refuses right judgment and just law, let him be forfeit to the one to whom <hi rend="spaced">it is due</hi>: if to the king, let him give him <hi rend="bold">40</hi> shillings, if to the earl <hi rend="bold">20</hi> shillings, if to the hundred <hi rend="bold">10</hi> shillings, if against all these, <hi rend="spaced">let him pay to all</hi>.

passages.text: Per legem Danorum lahslit reddat.
passages.en: By the law of the Danes let him pay <hi rend="italic">lahslit</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis alium iniuste<ptr n="4" target="IICn_16.lnote.oe.4-3"/> accusauerit, <hi rend="spaced">ita ut accusatus perditurus sit propter delationem</hi><ptr n="5" target="IICn_16.lnote.oe.5-2"/> accusantis pecuniam aut <hi rend="bold">uitam,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">et accusatus se</hi> inde<ptr n="6" target="IICn_16.lnote.oe.6"/> purgauerit<ptr n="7" target="IICn_16.lnote.oe.7"/>, <hi rend="spaced">delator</hi> sit reus<ptr n="8" target="IICn_16.lnote.oe.8-2"/> linguę suę, nisi <hi rend="spaced">persoluat delatum</hi> secundum pretium suum, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi><ptr n="9" target="IICn_16.lnote.oe.9-3"/> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">dicunt</hi>)</seg> be<ptr n="10" target="IICn_16.lnote.oe.10-2"/> his ƿere.<ptr n="11" target="IICn_16.lnote.oe.11-2"/>
passages.en: If anyone accuses another unjustly, <hi rend="spaced">so that the accused would lose through the denunciation</hi> of the accuser money or <hi rend="bold">life,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">and the accused</hi> clears <hi rend="spaced">himself</hi> of it, let the <hi rend="spaced">denouncer</hi> be liable for his tongue, unless he <hi rend="spaced">pays for the denounced</hi> according to his own price, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">say</hi>)</seg> <hi rend="italic">be his ƿere</hi> [by his wergeld].

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Constituantur</hi> <hi rend="bold">popularia</hi> placita<ptr n="12" target="IICn_17.lnote.oe.12-2"/>, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi> hundred<ptr n="13" target="IICn_17.lnote.oe.13-2"/>, sicut <hi rend="bold">iustum est et</hi><ptr n="*" target="IICn_17.lnote.oe.star"/><hi rend="bold"> ante hoc</hi><ptr n="14" target="IICn_17.lnote.oe.14"/><hi rend="bold"> factum est,</hi> super forisfacturam <hi rend="bold">quam lex docet;</hi> et nemo requirat regem, nisi non<ptr n="15" target="IICn_17.lnote.oe.15-2"/> possit habere<ptr n="16" target="IICn_17.lnote.oe.16-2"/> rectitudinem in hundredo suo.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">aus III Eg.</hi> 5? <hi rend="italic">Vgl. o. S.</hi> 197. 199
notes.en: from III Eg. 5? Cf. above pp. 197. 199

passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">Let</hi> <hi rend="bold">popular</hi> courts <hi rend="spaced">be established</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">hundred</hi>, as <hi rend="bold">is just and has been done before this,</hi> under the forfeiture <hi rend="bold">which the law teaches;</hi> and let no one apply to the king unless he cannot obtain right in his hundred.

passages.text: Ciuilia placita ter in anno teneantur, et comitatus bis in anno <hi rend="spaced">congregetur</hi>, nisi plus <hi rend="bold">necesse</hi> sit.
passages.en: Let civil courts be held three times a year, and the shire (court) <hi rend="spaced">be assembled</hi> twice a year, unless more be <hi rend="bold">necessary</hi>.

passages.text: Et in illo <hi rend="spaced">comitatu</hi> sint episcopus<ptr n="17" target="IICn_18-1.lnote.oe.17-2"/> et comes, qui <hi rend="spaced">ostendant</hi> populo et iusticias Dei et rectitudines saeculi.
passages.en: And at that <hi rend="spaced">shire court</hi> let there be the bishop and the earl, who are to <hi rend="spaced">show</hi> the people both the justices of God and the rights of the world.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> náme nec infra comitatum nec extra, antequam ter iusticiam in hundredo requirat. Nullus accipiat pro aliqua forisfactura quicquam quod Angli
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">náme</hi> [distraint] neither within the shire nor outside, before he has three times sought justice in the hundred. Let no one take for any forfeiture anything which the English

passages.text: Quodsi uice tertia rectum habere non poterit, eat ad comitatum <hi rend="bold">et ostendat, se iam tercio</hi><ptr n="1" target="IICn_19-1.lnote.oe.1-2"/><hi rend="bold"> hundredum adiisse, rectum</hi><ptr n="2" target="IICn_19-1.lnote.oe.2-4"/><hi rend="bold"> requisisse et habere non potuisse;</hi> tunc comitatus statuat illi<ptr n="3" target="IICn_19-1.lnote.oe.3-3"/> diem, <hi rend="bold">in quo qui calumniatur</hi><ptr n="4" target="IICn_19-1.lnote.oe.4-2"/><hi rend="bold"> faciat</hi><ptr n="5" target="IICn_19-1.lnote.oe.5-2"/><hi rend="bold"> rectum.</hi>
passages.en: But if the third time he cannot have right, let him go to the shire (court) <hi rend="bold">and show that he has now gone to the hundred three times, sought right and could not have it;</hi> then let the shire appoint him a day, <hi rend="bold">on which he who is accused shall do right.</hi>

passages.text: Quodsi <hi rend="spaced">dies statutus</hi> fractus fuerit, accepta<ptr n="6" target="IICn_19-2.lnote.oe.6"/> licentia a comitatu in <hi rend="spaced">eundo</hi> et in<ptr n="7" target="IICn_19-2.lnote.oe.7"/> redeundo, ut possit <hi rend="bold">accipere náme,</hi> quousque habeat sua.
passages.en: But if <hi rend="spaced">the appointed day</hi> is broken, leave having been received from the shire for <hi rend="spaced">going</hi> and returning, so that he may <hi rend="bold">take <hi rend="italic">náme</hi>,</hi> until he has his own.

passages.text: Constituimus etiam, ut omnis liber homo, qui uoluerit esse dignus <hi rend="spaced">purgatione et libertate</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">quod</hi><ptr n="8" target="IICn_20.lnote.oe.8-2"/> <hi rend="spaced">Angli uocant</hi><ptr n="9" target="IICn_20.lnote.oe.9"/> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">dicunt</hi>)</seg> lade þurþe ⁊ þeres þurþe, sit in hundredo et in <hi rend="bold">plegio;</hi> aliter si <hi rend="bold">occisus</hi> fuerit<ptr n="10" target="IICn_20.lnote.oe.10"/>, postquam fuerit<ptr n="11" target="IICn_20.lnote.oe.11"/> duodennis, non erit ulla<ptr n="12" target="IICn_20.lnote.oe.12"/> liberalitate<ptr n="13" target="IICn_20.lnote.oe.13-2"/> dignus.
passages.en: We also establish that every free man who wishes to be worthy of <hi rend="spaced">exculpation and freedom</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">which</hi> <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">say</hi>)</seg> <hi rend="italic">lade þurþe ⁊ þeres þurþe</hi> [worthy of exculpation and of wergeld], be in a hundred and in <hi rend="bold">pledge;</hi> otherwise, if he is <hi rend="bold">slain</hi> after he is twelve years old, he shall be worthy of no freeman's status.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Hoc quoque dicimus</hi> et de iis<ptr n="14" target="IICn_20a.lnote.oe.14"/> qui domum et <hi rend="spaced">terram</hi> habent et de iis<ptr n="15" target="IICn_20a.lnote.oe.15"/> qui <hi rend="spaced">non</hi><ptr n="16" target="IICn_20a.lnote.oe.16"/>, sed <hi rend="spaced">seruiunt</hi> aliis, quos<ptr n="17" target="IICn_20a.lnote.oe.17"/> Angli <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> husfæst<ptr n="18" target="IICn_20a.lnote.oe.18-2"/> ⁊ folgæres, ut omnes<ptr n="7" target="IICn_20a.lnote.oe.7-2"/> sint in hundredo et sub plegio, qui eos <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">teneat</hi><ptr n="19" target="IICn_20a.lnote.oe.19-2"/>)</seg> ad iusticiam habeat<ptr n="20" target="IICn_20a.lnote.oe.20-2"/>, <hi rend="bold">si aliquando calumniantur</hi><ptr n="21" target="IICn_20a.lnote.oe.21"/><hi rend="bold"> de aliqua</hi><ptr n="22" target="IICn_20a.lnote.oe.22"/><hi rend="bold"> re.</hi>

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">so Cb;</hi> hac [<hi rend="italic">verlesen aus</hi> hat] <hi rend="italic">H; fehlt übrigen</hi>
notes.en: thus Cb; hac [misread from hat] H; lacking in the others

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">über</hi> hac <hi rend="italic">von gleichz. Hd. H</hi>
notes.en: above hac in a contemporary hand H

passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">This too we say</hi> both of those who have house and <hi rend="spaced">land</hi> and of those who <hi rend="spaced">do not</hi>, but <hi rend="spaced">serve</hi> others, whom the English <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">husfæst ⁊ folgæres</hi> [householders and followers], that all be in a hundred and under pledge, which shall have <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">hold</hi>)</seg> them to justice, <hi rend="bold">if at any time they are accused of any matter.</hi>

passages.text: Multi fortes homines uolunt <hi rend="spaced">cum</hi><ptr n="23" target="IICn_20-1.lnote.oe.23"/> <hi rend="spaced">ingenio</hi> defendere in pla<hi rend="spaced">citis suos subiectos</hi><ptr n="24" target="IICn_20-1.lnote.oe.24"/>, quo leuius illis posse uidetur, pro seruis aut pro liberis; sed nos<ptr n="1" target="IICn_20-1.lnote.oe.1-5"/> huic iniusticie<ptr n="2" target="IICn_20-1.lnote.oe.2"/> consentire nolumus.

notes.de: d. c. ing. suos in p., quo <hi rend="italic">Lb</hi>
notes.en: d. c. ing. suos in p., quo Lb

passages.en: Many powerful men wish <hi rend="spaced">with</hi> <hi rend="spaced">cunning</hi> to defend in the cou<hi rend="spaced">rts their dependants</hi>, in whatever way seems to them easier to be able, for slaves or for free men; but we do not wish to consent to this injustice.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Propterea</hi> pręcipimus, ut omnis homo ultra <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">ętatem</hi><ptr n="3" target="IICn_21.lnote.oe.3-3"/>)</seg> duodecim annorum faciat sacramentum, quod nec latro uult esse nec latroni<ptr n="4" target="IICn_21.lnote.oe.4-2"/> consentire.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">Therefore</hi> we command that every man over <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">the age</hi>)</seg> of twelve years take an oath that he will neither be a thief nor be an accomplice of a thief.

passages.text: Si sit autem quisquam fidelis homo, qui <hi rend="spaced">iuste</hi> non fuerit<ptr n="5" target="IICn_22.lnote.oe.5-3"/> calumniatus <hi rend="spaced">de aliqua turpi</hi> re, et cui iuramentum non fregerit in<ptr n="6" target="IICn_22.lnote.oe.6-3"/> ore nec iudicium <hi rend="bold">ferri uel aquę,</hi> quod<ptr n="7" target="IICn_22.lnote.oe.7-2"/> <hi rend="spaced">Angli uocant</hi><ptr n="8" target="IICn_22.lnote.oe.8-2"/> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">dicunt</hi>)</seg> þa<hi rend="italic">m</hi> þe ue bærst<ptr n="9" target="IICn_22.lnote.oe.9-2"/> ne aþ ne ordel, <hi rend="spaced">iste talis, si aliquando calumniatus fuerit, purget se simplici</hi> purgatione.
passages.en: But if there is any trustworthy man, who has not <hi rend="spaced">rightly</hi> been accused <hi rend="spaced">of any shameful</hi> matter, and for whom neither the oath has broken in his mouth nor the ordeal <hi rend="bold">of iron or water,</hi> which <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">say</hi>)</seg> þa<hi rend="italic">m</hi> þe ue bærst ne aþ ne ordel [for whom neither oath nor ordeal has failed], <hi rend="spaced">such a one, if at any time he is accused, let him clear himself with simple</hi> purgation.

passages.text: Infideli autem homini eligatur iuramentum, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi><ptr n="10" target="IICn_22-1.lnote.oe.10-3"/> anfealdne<ptr n="11" target="IICn_22-1.lnote.oe.11-2"/> að, in hundredo<ptr n="12" target="IICn_22-1.lnote.oe.12-2"/>, et triplex iuramentum, sicut <hi rend="spaced">conuenit curię illi ad quam pertinet</hi>; aut<ptr n="13" target="IICn_22-1.lnote.oe.13"/> uadat<ptr n="14" target="IICn_22-1.lnote.oe.14"/> ad iudicium.

notes.en: o on an erasure H; -de Cb

passages.en: But for an untrustworthy man let a [selected] oath be chosen, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">anfealdne að</hi> [single oath], in the hundred, and a threefold oath, as <hi rend="spaced">befits that court to which he belongs</hi>; or let him go to the ordeal.

passages.text: Qui autem conquirere<ptr n="15" target="IICn_22-1a.lnote.oe.15-2"/> debet simplicem<ptr n="14" target="IICn_22-1a.lnote.oe.14-2"/> purgationem, simplici sacramento <hi rend="spaced">hoc faciat</hi>, <hi rend="bold">hoc est accipiat duos, et sit ipse tertius et sic iurando conquirat.</hi><ptr n="16" target="IICn_22-1a.lnote.oe.16"/> <hi rend="bold">Triplex</hi><ptr n="*" target="IICn_22-1a.lnote.oe.star-2"/><hi rend="bold"> uero</hi><ptr n="17" target="IICn_22-1a.lnote.oe.17"/><hi rend="bold"> iuramentum sic conquiratur: accipiat quinque et sit</hi><ptr n="18" target="IICn_22-1a.lnote.oe.18"/><hi rend="bold"> ipse sextus et sic iurando adquirat triplex iudicium aut triplex iuramentum.</hi><ptr n="19" target="IICn_22-1a.lnote.oe.19"/>

notes.de: iudicium uel <hi rend="italic">fügt zu Lb S</hi>
notes.en: iudicium uel added by Lb S

passages.en: But whoever must obtain simple purgation, let him <hi rend="spaced">do this</hi> with a simple oath, <hi rend="bold">that is, let him take two, and be himself the third, and so obtain it by swearing.</hi> <hi rend="bold">But a threefold oath is to be obtained thus: let him take five and be himself the sixth, and so by swearing acquire threefold ordeal or threefold oath.</hi>

passages.text: Si liberalis homo, id<ptr n="20" target="IICn_22-2.lnote.oe.20"/> est þegen<ptr n="21" target="IICn_22-2.lnote.oe.21"/>, habet fidelem hominem, <hi rend="spaced">qui pro eo possit iurare praeiuramentum</hi><ptr n="22" target="IICn_22-2.lnote.oe.22"/> <seg type="recension">(id<ptr n="23" target="IICn_22-2.lnote.oe.23"/> est foraþ)</seg>, ita sit; si autem non habet, ipsemet <hi rend="spaced">iuret</hi>.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">gleichzeitig übergeschr. H; fehlt Cb Lb S</hi>
notes.en: written above contemporaneously H; lacking in Cb Lb S

passages.en: If a free man of rank (thegn), that is <hi rend="italic">þegen</hi>, has a trustworthy man <hi rend="spaced">who can swear the fore-oath for him</hi> <seg type="recension">(that is <hi rend="italic">foraþ</hi>)</seg>, so be it; but if he does not have one, let him <hi rend="spaced">swear</hi> himself.

passages.text: Nec ei perdonetur<ptr n="1" target="IICn_22-3.lnote.oe.1-3"/> aliquod preiuramentum.<ptr n="2" target="IICn_22-3.lnote.oe.2-3"/>
passages.en: Nor shall any fore-oath be remitted to him.

passages.text: <hi rend="bold">Si latrocinium inuenitur in manu uel</hi><ptr n="3" target="IICn_23.lnote.oe.3-3"/><hi rend="bold"> in potestate alicuius, qui se non poterit excusare, si uult</hi> warantem<ptr n="4" target="IICn_23.lnote.oe.4-3"/> nominare, nullo modo ei<ptr n="5" target="IICn_23.lnote.oe.5-2"/> liceat, nisi habeat <hi rend="bold">duos</hi> idoneos testes, qui <hi rend="spaced">fuerint uidentes et audientes</hi>, unde sibi uenit quod <hi rend="spaced">in manu sua uel in potestate</hi> captum est.
passages.en: <hi rend="bold">If stolen goods are found in the hand or in the power of anyone who cannot excuse himself, if he wishes</hi> to name a warrantor, it shall in no way be allowed him, unless he has <hi rend="bold">two</hi> suitable witnesses who <hi rend="spaced">were seeing and hearing</hi> whence there came to him what was taken <hi rend="spaced">in his hand or in his power</hi>.

passages.text: Et ostendant testes hoc <hi rend="spaced">per sacramentum</hi>, quod iuste<ptr n="6" target="IICn_23-1.lnote.oe.6-4"/> sibi sunt<ptr n="7" target="IICn_23-1.lnote.oe.7-3"/> testes et <hi rend="spaced">fideles</hi>, sicut uidentes et audientes, in fide Dei et per fidem <hi rend="spaced">domini sui</hi>, quod iuste illud adquisiuit.
passages.en: And let the witnesses show this <hi rend="spaced">by oath</hi>, that they are rightly witnesses for him and <hi rend="spaced">trustworthy</hi>, as seeing and hearing, in the faith of God and by the faith <hi rend="spaced">of their lord</hi>, that he acquired it rightly.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Uolumus</hi> etiam, ut nullus emat aliquid ultra quattuor dena<hi rend="spaced">riorum</hi><ptr n="8" target="IICn_24.lnote.oe.8-2"/><hi rend="spaced"> ualens</hi>, nec rem uiuam nec<ptr n="9" target="IICn_24.lnote.oe.9-2"/> <hi rend="spaced">mortuam</hi> nec iacentem, sine quattuor<ptr n="10" target="IICn_24.lnote.oe.10-3"/> idoneis testibus, nec infra burgum nec <hi rend="spaced">extra</hi>.

notes.de: rem <hi rend="italic">fügt zu Cb</hi> [n. m. <hi rend="italic">richtige Erklärung zu</hi> n. i.]
notes.en: rem added by Cb [n. m. correct explanation of n. i.]

passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">We wish</hi> also that no one buy anything above four pe<hi rend="spaced">nce in value</hi>, neither a living thing nor a <hi rend="spaced">dead</hi> one nor a lying one, without four suitable witnesses, neither within a borough nor <hi rend="spaced">outside</hi>.

passages.text: Et si non <hi rend="spaced">tot nec tales</hi> testes habuerit, et aliquid tale <hi rend="spaced">in manu</hi> uel <hi rend="spaced">potestate eius</hi> inuentum fuerit, et ipse warantem<ptr n="11" target="IICn_24-1.lnote.oe.11-2"/> <hi rend="spaced">uoluerit uocare</hi>, non<ptr n="12" target="IICn_24-1.lnote.oe.12-3"/> ei ualeat <hi rend="spaced">neque</hi><ptr n="13" target="IICn_24-1.lnote.oe.13-2"/> liceat, sed reddatur calumnianti quod suum est — <hi rend="bold">aut ualens</hi> — et insuper iterum tantum ualens, et forisfacturam qui eam <hi rend="spaced">iuste</hi><ptr n="14" target="IICn_24-1.lnote.oe.14-2"/> habere debet.
passages.en: And if he does not have <hi rend="spaced">so many nor such</hi> witnesses, and some such thing is found <hi rend="spaced">in the hand</hi> or <hi rend="spaced">his power</hi>, and he <hi rend="spaced">wishes to vouch</hi> a warrantor, it shall not avail him <hi rend="spaced">nor</hi> be allowed, but let what is his be returned to the claimant — <hi rend="bold">or its value</hi> — and besides again as much in value, and the forfeiture [to him] who <hi rend="spaced">rightly</hi> ought to have it.

passages.text: Quodsi <hi rend="spaced">tales testes</hi> habuerit, quales supra diximus, warantem uocet; <hi rend="bold">et ille uocatus uocet</hi><ptr n="15" target="IICn_24-2.lnote.oe.15"/><hi rend="bold"> alium, si potest, et tertius adhuc tertium</hi><ptr n="*" target="IICn_24-2.lnote.oe.star-2"/><hi rend="bold"> uocet, si potest;</hi> et tertius<ptr n="**" target="IICn_24-2.lnote.oe.star2"/> suum faciet, <hi rend="spaced">si ualet; quodsi non ualet</hi>, reddatur ei, qui<ptr n="1" target="IICn_24-2.lnote.oe.1-2"/> iuste habere debet.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">bessere</hi> quartum; <hi rend="italic">doch zählt Inst. vielleicht die Gewähren.</hi>
notes.en: read quartum; but perhaps Inst. is counting the warrantors.

passages.en: But if he has <hi rend="spaced">such witnesses</hi> as we said above, let him vouch the warrantor; <hi rend="bold">and let the one vouched vouch another, if he can, and the third further vouch a third, if he can;</hi> and the third shall make it his own, <hi rend="spaced">if he is able; but if he is not able</hi>, let it be returned to him who rightly ought to have it.

passages.text: Nobis <hi rend="spaced">tamen</hi><ptr n="2" target="IICn_24-3.lnote.oe.2-4"/> iniustum uidetur, quod aliquis debeat sibi <hi rend="spaced">iurando</hi> uindicare<ptr n="3" target="IICn_24-3.lnote.oe.3-4"/>, <hi rend="spaced">quod iuste suum est</hi>, ubi testes sunt, et saltem ante sex menses, postquam furto ablatum est <hi rend="spaced">quod quęrit</hi>.
passages.en: To us <hi rend="spaced">however</hi> it seems unjust that anyone should claim for himself <hi rend="spaced">by swearing</hi> <hi rend="spaced">what is rightly his</hi>, where there are witnesses, and at least before six months after <hi rend="spaced">what he seeks</hi> was taken away by theft.

passages.text: Qui sepe calumniatus est de furto et <hi rend="bold">hundredum</hi><ptr n="4" target="IICn_25.lnote.oe.4-3"/> uocatus ter declinet: inueniantur de <hi rend="bold">hundredo</hi> qui eum adeant; et inueniat, si<ptr n="5" target="IICn_25.lnote.oe.5"/> potest, adhuc plegios.
passages.en: Whoever has often been accused of theft and, summoned [to] the <hi rend="bold">hundred</hi>, three times declines: let men be found from the <hi rend="bold">hundred</hi> who shall go to him; and let him find, if he can, sureties still.

passages.text: Quodsi non <hi rend="spaced">potuerit aut noluerit</hi>, capiatur aut<ptr n="6" target="IICn_25a.lnote.oe.6"/> uiuus aut mortuus et omnia quę habet.
passages.en: But if he <hi rend="spaced">could not or would not</hi>, let him be taken either alive or dead, and all that he has.

passages.text: Et <hi rend="spaced">inprimis</hi> reddatur calumnianti de<ptr n="7" target="IICn_25-1.lnote.oe.7"/> rebus latronis, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli uocant</hi> his ceapgeld<ptr n="8" target="IICn_25-1.lnote.oe.8"/>; et quod remanet <hi rend="spaced">diuidatur</hi> per medium inter hundredum et dominum <hi rend="spaced">latronis</hi>.

notes.en: d. r. l. lacking in S

passages.en: And <hi rend="spaced">first</hi> let there be returned to the claimant from the thief's goods [what] <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">his ceapgeld</hi> [his purchase-price]; and what remains <hi rend="spaced">let be divided</hi> in half between the hundred and the lord <hi rend="spaced">of the thief</hi>.

passages.text: Si autem parens <hi rend="spaced">illius latronis aut aliquis alius</hi> contradixerit adire <hi rend="spaced">illum</hi><ptr n="9" target="IICn_25-2.lnote.oe.9"/> latronem, sicut <hi rend="spaced">diximus</hi>, det regi <hi rend="bold">XL</hi><ptr n="*" target="IICn_25-2.lnote.oe.star"/> solidos.
passages.en: But if a kinsman <hi rend="spaced">of that thief or anyone else</hi> refuses to go against <hi rend="spaced">that</hi> thief, as <hi rend="spaced">we have said</hi>, let him give the king <hi rend="bold">40</hi> shillings.

passages.text: Publicus latro et traditor proprii<ptr n="10" target="IICn_26.lnote.oe.10"/> domini, <hi rend="spaced">quem Angli uocant</hi> hlaford<hi rend="bold">spice</hi><ptr n="11" target="IICn_26.lnote.oe.11"/>, quicquid re<hi rend="spaced">quisierint, nusquam uitam inueueniant</hi>.<ptr n="12" target="IICn_26.lnote.oe.12"/>
passages.en: A public thief and betrayer of his own lord, <hi rend="spaced">whom the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">hlaford</hi><hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">spice</hi></hi> [lord-traitor], whatever they re<hi rend="spaced">quest, let them nowhere find life</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis in placitis per contrarias calumnias uult defendere se ipsum aut hominem<ptr n="1" target="IICn_27.lnote.oe.1-6"/> suum, pro nichilo habeantur illę<ptr n="2" target="IICn_27.lnote.oe.2-4"/> calumnię, sed <hi rend="spaced">respondeat calumnianti se</hi>, sicut hundred iudicauerit.
passages.en: If anyone in the courts wishes to defend himself or his man by counter-accusations, let those accusations be held as nothing, but <hi rend="spaced">let him answer the one accusing him</hi>, as the <hi rend="italic">hundred</hi> shall judge.

passages.text: Nemo teneat aliquem hominem diutius <hi rend="spaced">tribus noctibus</hi>, nisi <hi rend="spaced">dominus eius</hi><ptr n="3" target="IICn_28.lnote.oe.3"/>, cui prius<ptr n="4" target="IICn_28.lnote.oe.4-2"/> seruiuit, eum commendauerit. <hi rend="bold">Quodsi aliter fecerit, persoluat priori</hi><ptr n="5" target="IICn_28.lnote.oe.5-2"/><hi rend="bold"> domino despectum eius et regi forisfacturam suam.</hi>
passages.en: Let no one keep any man longer than <hi rend="spaced">three nights</hi>, unless <hi rend="spaced">his lord</hi>, whom he served before, has commended him. <hi rend="bold">But if he does otherwise, let him pay the former lord his contempt-fine and the king his forfeiture.</hi>

passages.text: Nullus repellat a se seruientem suum, antequam sit purgatus de omni calumnia, unde fuit<ptr n="6" target="IICn_28-1.lnote.oe.6-2"/> prius calumniatus.
passages.en: Let no one put away from himself his servant before he is cleared of every accusation of which he was previously accused.

passages.text: Si cui latro occurrerit, et sine clamore sponte<ptr n="7" target="IICn_29.lnote.oe.7-2"/> illum abire permiserit, soluat latronem, <hi rend="bold">cui iustum est,</hi> prętio eiusdem latronis aut purget se pleno iuramento, quod eundem <hi rend="spaced">nesciuit esse latronem</hi>.<ptr n="8" target="IICn_29.lnote.oe.8-2"/>
passages.en: If a thief encounters anyone, and he willingly lets him go without hue and cry, let him pay for the thief, <hi rend="bold">to whom it is due,</hi> at the price of the same thief, or let him clear himself with a full oath that he <hi rend="spaced">did not know him to be a thief</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis est infidelis hundredo suo et sepe est<ptr n="9" target="IICn_30.lnote.oe.9"/> calumniatus, si <hi rend="spaced">simul uno die tribus calumniis</hi> proclamatus fuerit, triplici iudicio <hi rend="spaced">se purget</hi>.

notes.de: eo <hi rend="italic">Lb S;</hi> c. est <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: eo Lb S; c. est Cb

passages.en: If anyone is untrustworthy to his hundred and is often accused, if he is charged <hi rend="spaced">together on one day with three accusations</hi>, let him <hi rend="spaced">clear himself</hi> by threefold ordeal.

passages.text: Quodsi dominus<ptr n="10" target="IICn_30-1.lnote.oe.10"/> eius dixerit, quia <hi rend="spaced">nunquam illi</hi><ptr n="11" target="IICn_30-1.lnote.oe.11"/> fregerit iuramentum<ptr n="12" target="IICn_30-1.lnote.oe.12"/> <seg type="recension">(sacramentum)</seg> nec iudicium, nec prętium latrocinii persoluit, tunc ille dominus accipiat secum duos fideles et hoc<ptr n="1" target="IICn_30-1.lnote.oe.1-6"/> <hi rend="spaced">ita esse sacramento affirmet</hi>, nisi talem prępositum habeat, qui dignus sit hoc idem <hi rend="spaced">pro eo facere</hi>.<ptr n="2" target="IICn_30-1.lnote.oe.2-3"/>
passages.en: But if his lord says that <hi rend="spaced">never for him</hi> has oath <seg type="recension">(sworn oath)</seg> or ordeal broken, nor has he paid the price of theft, then let that lord take with him two trustworthy men and <hi rend="spaced">affirm by oath that it is so</hi>, unless he has such a reeve as is worthy <hi rend="spaced">to do this same for him</hi>.

passages.text: Si sacramentum bene processerit<ptr n="3" target="IICn_30-2.lnote.oe.3"/>, <hi rend="spaced">ille calumniatus eligat</hi>, quid<ptr n="4" target="IICn_30-2.lnote.oe.4"/> horum<ptr n="5" target="IICn_30-2.lnote.oe.5"/> uoluerit, aut simplex iudicium<ptr n="6" target="IICn_30-2.lnote.oe.6"/> aut sacramentum <hi rend="bold">XX</hi><ptr n="*" target="IICn_30-2.lnote.oe.star"/><hi rend="bold"> solidorum</hi> in tribus hundredis, ultra XXXta denarios.

notes.en: cf. I Cn. 3, 2 M S Cb

passages.en: If the oath goes well, let <hi rend="spaced">the accused choose</hi> which of these he wishes, either simple ordeal or an oath <hi rend="bold">of 20 shillings</hi> in three hundreds, above 30 pence.

passages.text: Quodsi non <hi rend="spaced">audent</hi><ptr n="7" target="IICn_30-3.lnote.oe.7"/> sacramentum facere, eat<ptr n="8" target="IICn_30-3.lnote.oe.8"/> ad triplex iudicium.
passages.en: But if they <hi rend="spaced">dare</hi> not make the oath, let him go to the threefold ordeal.

passages.text: Ita<ptr n="9" target="IICn_30-3a.lnote.oe.9"/> autem <hi rend="spaced">adquiratur</hi> illud<ptr n="10" target="IICn_30-3a.lnote.oe.10"/> triplex iudicium <seg type="recension">(quod<ptr n="11" target="IICn_30-3a.lnote.oe.11"/> <hi rend="spaced">Angli dicunt</hi> ‘<hi rend="bold">ofræce</hi> <hi rend="italic">þæt</hi> ordel')</seg>: accipiat secum quinque et sit ipse sextus; <hi rend="spaced">ita enim</hi><ptr n="12" target="IICn_30-3a.lnote.oe.12"/> conquiritur triplex iudicium.

notes.de: quod — ordel <hi rend="italic">nur H am Rande</hi>
notes.en: quod — ordel only H, in the margin

passages.en: Thus <hi rend="spaced">is to be obtained</hi> that threefold ordeal <seg type="recension">(which <hi rend="spaced">the English call</hi> ‘<hi rend="bold">ofræce</hi> <hi rend="italic">þæt</hi> ordel')</seg>: let him take with him five and be himself the sixth; <hi rend="spaced">for thus</hi> is threefold ordeal obtained.

passages.text: Quodsi reus fuerit et in iudicio <hi rend="spaced">ceciderit</hi>, prima uice ante<ptr n="13" target="IICn_30-3b.lnote.oe.13"/> alia reddat <hi rend="spaced">calumniantibus</hi> dupliciter sua, et dominis<ptr n="14" target="IICn_30-3b.lnote.oe.14"/> illorum <hi rend="spaced">pretium eorum</hi>, et postea <hi rend="spaced">inueniant</hi><ptr n="15" target="IICn_30-3b.lnote.oe.15"/> fideiussores, quod deinde <hi rend="spaced">cessabunt</hi>.<ptr n="16" target="IICn_30-3b.lnote.oe.16-2"/>
passages.en: But if he is guilty and <hi rend="spaced">fails</hi> in the ordeal, the first time let him before other things repay <hi rend="spaced">the accusers</hi> double what is theirs, and to their lords <hi rend="spaced">their price</hi>, and afterwards let them <hi rend="spaced">find</hi> sureties that they will thenceforth <hi rend="spaced">desist</hi>.

passages.text: Si secundo<ptr n="17" target="IICn_30-4.lnote.oe.17"/> <hi rend="spaced">ceciderint</hi><ptr n="18" target="IICn_30-4.lnote.oe.18"/>, abscidantur illis manus aut pedes <hi rend="spaced">aut utrumque, si culpa tanta</hi> fuerit.<ptr n="19" target="IICn_30-4.lnote.oe.19"/>
passages.en: If they <hi rend="spaced">fail</hi> a second time, let their hands or feet be cut off, <hi rend="spaced">or both, if the guilt be so great</hi>.

passages.text: Quodsi adhuc maiora fecerit, eruantur sibi oculi, et auferatur sibi<ptr n="20" target="IICn_30-5.lnote.oe.20"/> nasus cum labro et aures aut corium capitis cum capillis, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> <hi rend="bold">behætian</hi><ptr n="1" target="IICn_30-5.lnote.oe.1-6"/>; sic possunt <hi rend="spaced">latrones</hi> corrigi et <hi rend="spaced">animę</hi> saluari.

notes.en: -ættie added later Cb; -hedian S; bihedian Lb

passages.en: But if he has done still greater things, let his eyes be put out, and his nose be taken off with the lip, and the ears, or the skin of the head with the hair, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">behætian</hi></hi> [to scalp]; thus can <hi rend="spaced">thieves</hi> be corrected and <hi rend="spaced">souls</hi> saved.

passages.text: Quodsi <hi rend="spaced">calumniatus euaserit</hi> et iudicium declinauerit, fideiussores <hi rend="spaced">reddant calumnianti</hi> quod á <hi rend="spaced">latrone</hi> exegit, et regi<ptr n="2" target="IICn_30-6.lnote.oe.2"/> prętium <hi rend="spaced">latronis</hi> aut illi qui habet <hi rend="bold">sacę</hi><ptr n="3" target="IICn_30-6.lnote.oe.3-2"/><hi rend="bold"> et socne.</hi>

notes.de: sac̄ <hi rend="italic">Cb;</hi> sache et sochen <hi rend="italic">Lb. Vgl.</hi> 37 <hi rend="italic">Hs. G</hi>
notes.en: sac̄ Cb; sache et sochen Lb. Cf. 37 M S G

passages.en: But if the <hi rend="spaced">accused escapes</hi> and avoids the ordeal, the sureties are to <hi rend="spaced">pay back to the accuser</hi> what he claimed from the <hi rend="spaced">thief</hi>, and to the king the price of the <hi rend="spaced">thief</hi>, or to him who has <hi rend="bold">sake and soke.</hi>

passages.text: Quodsi dominus latronis inculpatus fuerit, quasi sponte illum ire <hi rend="spaced">permiserit</hi><ptr n="4" target="IICn_30-7.lnote.oe.4"/>, acceptis quinque <hi rend="spaced">fidelibus hominibus</hi> purget se, <hi rend="spaced">si potest</hi>.
passages.en: But if the lord of the thief is accused, as though he willingly <hi rend="spaced">let</hi> him go, taking five <hi rend="spaced">trustworthy men</hi> let him clear himself, <hi rend="spaced">if he can</hi>.

passages.text: Si se purgauerit, illi<ptr n="5" target="IICn_30-8.lnote.oe.5"/> detur <hi rend="spaced">prętium latronis, id est</hi> ƿere.
passages.en: If he clears himself, let there be given to him the <hi rend="spaced">price of the thief, that is,</hi> the <hi rend="italic">ƿere</hi>.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">purgare</hi> se<ptr n="6" target="IICn_30-9.lnote.oe.6"/> non poterit, rex habeat illud<ptr n="7" target="IICn_30-9.lnote.oe.7"/> prętium<ptr n="8" target="IICn_30-9.lnote.oe.8"/>; et latro habeatur <hi rend="spaced">exul et reus</hi> ab omni populo.
passages.en: If he cannot <hi rend="spaced">clear</hi> himself, let the king have that price; and let the thief be held <hi rend="spaced">an outlaw and guilty</hi> by all the people.

passages.text: Omnis dominus habeat familiam suam in proprio plegio <seg type="recension">(suo<ptr n="9" target="IICn_31.lnote.oe.9"/>)</seg>, ut, si aliquis <hi rend="spaced">illorum</hi> calumniatus fuerit, respondeat hundredo, in quo calumniatus est, sicut iustum sit.

notes.en: so Cb Lb; omitted in the others

passages.en: Every lord is to have his household in his own <seg type="recension">(his)</seg> pledge, so that, if any <hi rend="spaced">of them</hi> is accused, he answers to the <hi rend="italic">hundred</hi> in which he is accused, as is right.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">post</hi><ptr n="10" target="IICn_31-1.lnote.oe.10"/> calumniam euaserit, dominus soluat<ptr n="11" target="IICn_31-1.lnote.oe.11-2"/> eius ƿere<ptr n="12" target="IICn_31-1.lnote.oe.12"/> regi, <hi rend="bold">et plegii quod calumniatus est. Si autem infra annum et unum diem dominus eius illum capere</hi><ptr n="13" target="IICn_31-1.lnote.oe.13"/><hi rend="bold"> poterit, recipiat hoc quod pro eo dedit.</hi>

notes.de: queat c. <hi rend="italic">statt</hi> c. p. <hi rend="italic">Lb</hi>
notes.en: queat c. instead of c. p. Lb

passages.en: If he escapes <hi rend="spaced">after</hi> the accusation, the lord is to pay his <hi rend="italic">ƿere</hi> to the king, <hi rend="bold">and to the pledges what he was accused of. But if within a year and a day his lord can catch him, he is to get back what he gave for him.</hi>

passages.text: Et si ipse dominus calumniatus fuerit, quod eum sponte fugere permiserit, <hi rend="bold">si ille est</hi><ptr n="1" target="IICn_31-1a.lnote.oe.1-6"/><hi rend="bold"> liberalis,</hi> id <hi rend="spaced">est þegen</hi>, acceptis quinque similibus purget se.
passages.en: And if the lord himself is accused of having let him flee willingly, <hi rend="bold">if he is a free man of rank,</hi> that <hi rend="spaced">is a <hi rend="italic">þegen</hi></hi> [thegn], taking five of his like let him clear himself.

passages.text: Si non <hi rend="spaced">poterit</hi><ptr n="2" target="IICn_31-2.lnote.oe.2"/> purgare<ptr n="3" target="IICn_31-2.lnote.oe.3-2"/> se, persoluat regi ƿere suum; et homo sit exul <hi rend="spaced">ab omnibus</hi>.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">fehlt Cb, wo nachträglich</hi> potest <hi rend="italic">hinter</hi> se
notes.en: omitted Cb, where potest has been added later after se

passages.en: If he <hi rend="spaced">cannot</hi> clear himself, let him pay the king his <hi rend="italic">ƿere</hi>; and the man is to be an outlaw <hi rend="spaced">from all</hi>.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">seruus ceciderit</hi> in iudicio <hi rend="bold">ferri aut</hi><ptr n="4" target="IICn_32.lnote.oe.4-2"/><hi rend="bold"> aquę,</hi> <hi rend="spaced">criminis</hi> signum prima uice fiet ei.
passages.en: If a <hi rend="spaced">slave fails</hi> in the ordeal <hi rend="bold">of iron or water,</hi> a mark <hi rend="spaced">of crime</hi> is to be made on him the first time.

passages.text: Si secundo ceciderit, nichil<ptr n="5" target="IICn_32-1.lnote.oe.5"/> aliud <hi rend="spaced">emendationis</hi> accipiatur, nisi ut ei<ptr n="6" target="IICn_32-1.lnote.oe.6-4"/> caput <hi rend="spaced">abscidatur</hi>.
passages.en: If he fails a second time, let nothing else be accepted <hi rend="spaced">by way of amends</hi>, except that his head <hi rend="spaced">be cut off</hi>.

passages.text: Qui omni populo infidelis est, prępositus regis ponat eum sub fideiussoribus, ut custodiant illum<ptr n="7" target="IICn_33.lnote.oe.7"/> ad iusticiam.
passages.en: Whoever is untrustworthy to all the people, the king's reeve is to put him under sureties, so that they keep him to justice.

passages.text: Et si non <hi rend="spaced">potest</hi><ptr n="8" target="IICn_33-1.lnote.oe.8"/> habere plegios, occidatur et in loco latronum sepeliatur.
passages.en: And if he <hi rend="spaced">cannot</hi> have pledges, let him be killed and buried in the place of thieves.

passages.text: Quod si forte<ptr n="9" target="IICn_33-1a.lnote.oe.9"/> aliquis eum ui<ptr n="10" target="IICn_33-1a.lnote.oe.10"/> defendere uoluerit, habeat eandem legem.

notes.de: a. f. <hi rend="italic">Cb; fehlt Lb S</hi>
notes.en: a. f. Cb; omitted Lb S

passages.en: But if perhaps anyone wishes to defend him by force, let him have the same law.

passages.text: Et qui hec supersederit et ista facere noluerit, sicut nos omnes simul<ptr n="11" target="IICn_33-2.lnote.oe.11"/> <hi rend="spaced">condiximus</hi>, det regi <hi rend="bold">quadraginta</hi><ptr n="12" target="IICn_33-2.lnote.oe.12-2"/> solidos.
passages.en: And whoever neglects these things and will not do them, as we all together <hi rend="spaced">agreed</hi>, let him give the king <hi rend="bold">forty</hi> shillings.

passages.text: Et sit<ptr n="13" target="IICn_34.lnote.oe.13"/> inter <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">omnes</hi><ptr n="14" target="IICn_34.lnote.oe.14"/>)</seg> ciuitates una lex et una purgatio.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">fehlt Cb, wo hinter</hi> purg. <hi rend="italic">später</hi> sit
notes.en: omitted Cb, where sit has been added later after purg.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">nur Cb, wo</hi> uel ciuitates <hi rend="italic">über</hi> ciues<hi rend="italic">; fehlt übr.</hi>
notes.en: only Cb, where uel ciuitates is written above ciues; omitted in the others

passages.en: And let there be among <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">all</hi>)</seg> the towns one law and one purgation.

passages.text: Si aduena aut peregrinus, qui de longinquo uenit, sit tribulatus pro penuria amicorum, ut non possit habere plegios, ad primam calumniam, tunc subeat captionem <hi rend="bold">regis</hi> et ibi expectet<ptr n="1" target="IICn_35.lnote.oe.1-5"/>, quoad usque<ptr n="2" target="IICn_35.lnote.oe.2-4"/> uadat ad iudicium <hi rend="bold">ferri aut</hi><ptr n="3" target="IICn_35.lnote.oe.3-2"/><hi rend="bold"> aquę</hi> illicque inueniat quod potest.

notes.de: et <hi rend="italic">später verbessert</hi> uel <hi rend="italic">Cb;</hi> uel <hi rend="italic">Lb</hi>
notes.en: et later corrected to uel Cb; uel Lb

passages.en: If a stranger or foreigner, who comes from afar, is in difficulty for lack of friends, so that he cannot have pledges, at the first accusation, then let him undergo the <hi rend="bold">king's</hi> custody and wait there until he goes to the ordeal <hi rend="bold">of iron or water</hi> and there find what he can.

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">Certe dico uobis</hi>, si quis extraneo aut peregrino de longe uenienti <hi rend="spaced">aliud</hi> iudicium<ptr n="4" target="IICn_35-1.lnote.oe.4-3"/> iudicauerit, sibi<ptr n="5" target="IICn_35-1.lnote.oe.5-3"/> ipsi<ptr n="4" target="IICn_35-1.lnote.oe.4-3"/> nocet.<ptr n="6" target="IICn_35-1.lnote.oe.6"/>
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">Truly I tell you</hi>, if anyone judges a <hi rend="spaced">different</hi> judgement for a stranger or foreigner coming from afar, he harms himself.

passages.text: Si quis periurium fecerit <hi rend="bold">super textum euangelil aut</hi> super reliquias sanctorum et uictus fuerit, <hi rend="spaced">quod iniuste iurauerit</hi>, careat <hi rend="spaced">manibus</hi> aut det dimidium prętii<ptr n="7" target="IICn_36.lnote.oe.7-4"/> sui ipsius; et hoc diuidatur inter episcopum et dominum ipsius hominis.

notes.en: altered to prętium H; pretium Di

passages.en: If anyone commits perjury <hi rend="bold">on the text of the Gospel or</hi> on the relics of the saints and is convicted <hi rend="spaced">of having sworn unjustly</hi>, let him lose his <hi rend="spaced">hands</hi> or give half of his own price; and this is to be divided between the bishop and the lord of that man.

passages.text: Et post hoc non sit dignus iuramenti, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> aðes þyrðe<ptr n="8" target="IICn_36-1.lnote.oe.8"/>, nisi altius Deo satisfaciat et fideiussores inueniat, quod amplius cessauerit.
passages.en: And after this let him not be worthy of an oath, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">aðes þyrðe</hi>, unless he makes satisfaction to God more deeply and finds sureties that he will cease henceforth.

passages.text: Qui uero steterit in falso testimonio et uictus fuerit, <hi rend="spaced">quod</hi> ita sit<ptr n="9" target="IICn_37.lnote.oe.9"/>, non sit amplius dignus stare aut <hi rend="spaced">portare testimonium</hi>, <hi rend="bold">quia legalitatem suam perdidit</hi><ptr n="10" target="IICn_37.lnote.oe.10-2"/>, et ideo persoluat regi aut domino terrę <hi rend="bold">X solidos,</hi> quod <hi rend="bold">Dani</hi> <hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi> halsfang.<ptr n="11" target="IICn_37.lnote.oe.11"/>
passages.en: But whoever stands in false witness and is convicted <hi rend="spaced">that</hi> it is so, let him no longer be worthy to stand or <hi rend="spaced">bear witness</hi>, <hi rend="bold">because he has lost his lawfulness</hi>, and therefore let him pay to the king or to the lord of the land <hi rend="bold">X shillings,</hi> which the <hi rend="bold">Danes</hi> <hi rend="spaced">call</hi> <hi rend="italic">halsfang</hi>.

passages.text: Si quis <hi rend="spaced">aliquem de</hi><ptr n="1" target="IICn_39.lnote.oe.1-4"/> seruitoribus altaris occiderit, sit exul contra Deum<ptr n="2" target="IICn_39.lnote.oe.2-3"/> et contra <hi rend="spaced">omnes</hi> homines, nisi per<ptr n="3" target="IICn_39.lnote.oe.3-2"/> exilium altius emendet, et parentibus etiam; aut purget se purgatione, <hi rend="spaced">quam Angli uocant</hi> ƿerelade.<ptr n="4" target="IICn_39.lnote.oe.4-2"/>
passages.en: If anyone kills <hi rend="spaced">one of the</hi> servants of the altar, let him be an outlaw before God and before <hi rend="spaced">all</hi> men, unless he makes amends more deeply through exile, and to the kinsmen also; or let him clear himself with the purgation <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">ƿerelade</hi>.

passages.text: Et infra triginta dies incipiat pęnitentiam et emendationem contra Deum et homines.
passages.en: And within thirty days let him begin penance and amends towards God and men.

passages.text: Si quis ordinatum aut alienum per consilium suum perdere fecerit pecuniam aut uitam, tunc debet esse<ptr n="5" target="IICn_40.lnote.oe.5"/> rex illi pro parente et pro <hi rend="spaced">domino</hi>, nisi alium habeat.
passages.en: If anyone through his counsel causes a man in orders or a stranger to lose money or life, then the king must be to him for kinsman and for <hi rend="spaced">lord</hi>, unless he has another.

passages.text: Et<ptr n="6" target="IICn_40-1.lnote.oe.6"/> emendetur regi secundum quod iustum est, aut ipse rex districte uindicet <hi rend="spaced">quod factum est</hi>,
passages.en: And let amends be made to the king according to what is right, or let the king himself strictly avenge <hi rend="spaced">what has been done</hi>,

passages.text: <hi rend="spaced">quia</hi> Christiano regi conuenit et decet, ut acriter<ptr n="7" target="IICn_40-2.lnote.oe.7"/> uindicet in <hi rend="spaced">eos qui leges Dei uiolant</hi>.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">because</hi> it befits and becomes a Christian king that he sharply take vengeance on <hi rend="spaced">those who violate the laws of God</hi>.

passages.text: Si minister altaris homicidium fecerit aut aliquod magnum scelus, careat et ordine et <hi rend="spaced">liberalitate</hi><ptr n="8" target="IICn_41.lnote.oe.8-2"/> sua<ptr n="9" target="IICn_41.lnote.oe.9-2"/> et uadat in exilium, secundum quod<ptr n="10" target="IICn_41.lnote.oe.10-2"/> papa sibi<ptr n="11" target="IICn_41.lnote.oe.11"/> constituerit.

notes.de: dominus <hi rend="italic">fügt zu Lb;</hi> qu. do. proprius s. <hi rend="italic">S</hi>
notes.en: dominus added by Lb; qu. do. proprius s. S

passages.en: If a minister of the altar commits homicide or some great crime, let him lose both his order and his <hi rend="spaced">rank</hi> and go into exile, according to what the pope appoints for him.

passages.text: Quodsi purgare se<ptr n="12" target="IICn_41-1.lnote.oe.12"/> uoluerit, triplici<ptr n="13" target="IICn_41-1.lnote.oe.13"/> <hi rend="spaced">sacramento</hi> se purget.
passages.en: But if he wishes to clear himself, let him clear himself with a threefold <hi rend="spaced">oath</hi>.

passages.text: Et nisi infra triginta dies emendationem inceperit et Deo et ho<hi rend="spaced">minibus satisfecerit, expellatur a terra</hi> et sit exul.
passages.en: And unless within thirty days he has begun amends and to both God and <hi rend="spaced">men made satisfaction, let him be driven from the land</hi> and be an outlaw.

passages.text: Si quis aliquem ordinatum ligauerit aut ceciderit<ptr n="14" target="IICn_42.lnote.oe.14"/> aut turpiter deriserit, emendet illi secundum quod iustum est — <hi rend="bold">scilicet secundum modum ordinis</hi> —, et<ptr n="1" target="IICn_42.lnote.oe.1-5"/> episcopo altaris<ptr n="2" target="IICn_42.lnote.oe.2-5"/> emendationem, <hi rend="spaced">quod dicitur</hi> þeofodbote<ptr n="3" target="IICn_42.lnote.oe.3-2"/>, et domino aut regi plenum despectum, <hi rend="spaced">omnia ista</hi> secundum modum ordinis; aut purget se plena purgatione.<ptr n="4" target="IICn_42.lnote.oe.4-2"/>

notes.de: cic. <hi rend="italic">Di;</hi> turp. d. aut c. <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: cic. Di; turp. d. aut c. Cb

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">statt c.</hi> 43 <hi rend="italic">s. o.</hi> I 5<hi rend="italic">aa</hi>
notes.en: for cap. 43 see above I 5<hi rend="italic">aa</hi>

passages.en: If anyone binds or beats or shamefully mocks someone in orders, let him make amends to him according to what is right — <hi rend="bold">namely according to the measure of his order</hi> —, and to the bishop the altar-amends, <hi rend="spaced">which is called</hi> <hi rend="italic">þeofodbote</hi>, and to the lord or the king the full contempt-fine, <hi rend="spaced">all these</hi> according to the measure of the order; or let him clear himself with full purgation.

passages.text: Si quis latro <hi rend="spaced">aut alius</hi><ptr n="5" target="IICn_44.lnote.oe.5-2"/> condemnatus ad mortem quęrit confessionem, nullo modo ei denegetur.
passages.en: If a thief <hi rend="spaced">or another</hi> condemned to death seeks confession, let it in no way be denied him.

passages.text: Quod si <hi rend="spaced">quis fecerit</hi>, regi emendet<ptr n="6" target="IICn_44-1.lnote.oe.6-2"/>; aut purget se sexto.
passages.en: But if <hi rend="spaced">anyone does so</hi>, let him make amends to the king; or clear himself as one of six.

passages.text: Nullus <hi rend="spaced">latro aut</hi><ptr n="7" target="IICn_45.lnote.oe.7-3"/> morte condemnatus die Dominico <hi rend="bold">aut</hi><ptr n="8" target="IICn_45.lnote.oe.8"/><hi rend="bold"> alio</hi><ptr n="9" target="IICn_45.lnote.oe.9"/><hi rend="bold"> aliquo die</hi><ptr n="10" target="IICn_45.lnote.oe.10"/><hi rend="bold"> festiuo</hi> occidatur, nisi fugere aut pugnare <hi rend="spaced">uoluerit</hi>; sed custodiatur, quoad<ptr n="11" target="IICn_45.lnote.oe.11"/> usque<ptr n="12" target="IICn_45.lnote.oe.12"/> festiuitas transeat.

notes.de: f. di. <hi rend="italic">Lb S;</hi> festo <hi rend="italic">ohne</hi> die <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: f. di. Lb S; festo without die Cb

passages.en: Let no <hi rend="spaced">thief or</hi> man condemned to death be killed on the Lord's day <hi rend="bold">or on any other feast day</hi>, unless he <hi rend="spaced">wishes</hi> to flee or fight; but let him be guarded until the feast passes.

passages.text: Si liber<ptr n="13" target="IICn_45-1.lnote.oe.13"/> homo festiuo die operetur<ptr n="14" target="IICn_45-1.lnote.oe.14"/> et <hi rend="spaced">ita festiuitatem uiolauerit</hi>, <hi rend="bold">decem</hi><ptr n="15" target="IICn_45-1.lnote.oe.15"/><hi rend="bold"> solidos</hi> persoluat, et tamen Deo satisfaciat.

notes.en: quilibet, in the margin liber Cb

passages.en: If a free man works on a feast day and <hi rend="spaced">so violates the feast</hi>, let him pay <hi rend="bold">ten shillings</hi>, and nonetheless make satisfaction to God.

passages.text: Si seruus <hi rend="spaced">hoc faciat</hi>, careat corio suo aut emendet secundum modum operis.
passages.en: If a slave <hi rend="spaced">does this</hi>, let him lose his hide or make amends according to the measure of the deed.

passages.text: Sin autem <hi rend="spaced">inuitus</hi>, domino suo <hi rend="spaced">pręcipiente</hi>, hoc fecerit, dominus careat seruo illo<ptr n="1" target="IICn_45-3.lnote.oe.1-5"/> et det <hi rend="bold">halsfang;</hi> seruus autem sit omnino liber; aut dominus purget<ptr n="2" target="IICn_45-3.lnote.oe.2-3"/> se.

notes.en: lacking in Cb, where halsfans stands

passages.en: But if he did this <hi rend="spaced">unwilling</hi>, at his lord's <hi rend="spaced">command</hi>, let the lord lose that slave and give <hi rend="bold"><hi rend="italic">halsfang</hi>;</hi> and let the slave be wholly free; or let the lord clear himself.

passages.text: Si liber<ptr n="5" target="IICn_46.lnote.oe.5"/> homo ieiunium uiolauerit, secundum Danos lahslit<ptr n="4" target="IICn_46.lnote.oe.4"/> <seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(id est X solidos)</hi></seg> reddat, secundum Anglos<ptr n="5" target="IICn_46.lnote.oe.5"/> ad qualitatem <hi rend="spaced">ieiunii</hi>.

notes.de: X s., i. halslit <hi rend="italic">Cb;</hi> i. X s. <hi rend="italic">übergeschr. H; fehlt Di Lb; am Rande</hi> XX s. <hi rend="italic">Di</hi>
notes.en: X s., i. halslit Cb; i. X s. written above H; lacking in Di Lb; XX s. in the margin Di

passages.en: If a free man breaks a fast, according to the Danes let him pay <hi rend="italic">lahslit</hi> <seg type="recension"><hi rend="bold">(that is, X shillings)</hi></seg>, according to the English by the nature <hi rend="spaced">of the fast</hi>.

passages.text: Si <hi rend="spaced">seruus</hi> ieiunium uiolauerit carnem manducando, uerberetur secundum modum culpę.
passages.en: If a <hi rend="spaced">slave</hi> breaks a fast by eating meat, let him be beaten according to the measure of the fault.

passages.text: Si quis uiolauerit ieiunium quadragesimale<ptr n="6" target="IICn_47.lnote.oe.6-2"/> aut pugnando aut rapiendo<ptr n="7" target="IICn_47.lnote.oe.7-2"/> aut mulierem <hi rend="spaced">ducendo</hi> aut aliquid mali magni faciendo, dupliciter emendet secundum emendationem operis <hi rend="spaced">uiolatę</hi> festiuitatis.

notes.de: al. m. m. f. aut ra. aut mu. duc., dup. <hi rend="italic">Di</hi>
notes.en: al. m. m. f. aut ra. aut mu. duc., dup. Di

passages.en: If anyone violates the Lenten fast either by fighting or by robbing or by <hi rend="spaced">marrying</hi> a woman or by doing some great evil, let him make double amends according to the amends for the deed of a <hi rend="spaced">violated</hi> feast.

passages.text: Et <hi rend="spaced">si negauerit</hi>, triplici purgatione<ptr n="8" target="IICn_47-1.lnote.oe.8"/> id neget.
passages.en: And <hi rend="spaced">if he denies it</hi>, let him deny it with a threefold purgation.

passages.text: Si quis aliquam ęcclesiasticarum rectitudinum armis defenderit, <hi rend="bold">decem solidos</hi><ptr n="9" target="IICn_48.lnote.oe.9"/> secundum Danos emendet<ptr n="10" target="IICn_48.lnote.oe.10-2"/>; si negauerit, accipiat undecim<ptr n="11" target="IICn_48.lnote.oe.11-2"/> et ipse sit duodecimus et <hi rend="spaced">ita se purget</hi>.

notes.de: XII ei i. s. XIII<sup>mus</sup> <hi rend="italic">Lb S</hi>
notes.en: XII ei i. s. XIII<sup>mus</sup> Lb S

passages.en: If anyone defends any of the church's rights with arms, let him make amends of <hi rend="bold">ten shillings</hi> according to the Danes; if he denies it, let him take eleven and himself be the twelfth and <hi rend="spaced">so clear himself</hi>.

passages.text: Quodsi ibi<ptr n="12" target="IICn_48-1.lnote.oe.12-2"/> <hi rend="spaced">aliquem</hi><ptr n="13" target="IICn_48-1.lnote.oe.13"/> uulnerauerit, id <hi rend="spaced">illi</hi> emendet cui <hi rend="spaced">uulnus</hi> fecit, et domino <hi rend="spaced">illius plenam</hi> forisfacturam, et <hi rend="spaced">manum suam</hi> ab episcopo redimat aut perdat.
passages.en: But if he wounds <hi rend="spaced">anyone</hi> there, let him make amends for it <hi rend="spaced">to him</hi> on whom he inflicted the <hi rend="spaced">wound</hi>, and to the lord <hi rend="spaced">of that man the full</hi> forfeiture, and let him redeem <hi rend="spaced">his hand</hi> from the bishop or lose it.

passages.text: Et si hominem occiderit, sit exul et cum clamore expellatur <hi rend="spaced">ab omnibus</hi><ptr n="1" target="IICn_48-2.lnote.oe.1-4"/> <hi rend="spaced">qui Dei iusticiam</hi> uolunt<ptr n="2" target="IICn_48-2.lnote.oe.2-4"/>.
passages.en: And if he kills a man, let him be an outlaw and be driven out with hue and cry <hi rend="spaced">by all</hi> <hi rend="spaced">who</hi> want <hi rend="spaced">God's justice</hi>.

passages.text: Et si <hi rend="spaced">ipse</hi> occisus<ptr n="3" target="IICn_48-3.lnote.oe.3-3"/> fuerit, <hi rend="spaced">propterea</hi><ptr n="4" target="IICn_48-3.lnote.oe.4-3"/> quia contra iusticiam pugnauerit, iaceat impersolutus, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi><ptr n="5" target="IICn_48-3.lnote.oe.5-2"/> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">uocant</hi>)</seg> ægylde.<ptr n="6" target="IICn_48-3.lnote.oe.6-2"/>

notes.en: di. H Di; u. the others

notes.de: ægilde <hi rend="italic">Di;</hi> igilde <hi rend="italic">S;</hi> eðgelde <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: ægilde Di; igilde S; eðgelde Cb

passages.en: And if <hi rend="spaced">he himself</hi> is killed, <hi rend="spaced">for the reason</hi> that he fought against justice, let him lie unpaid for, <hi rend="spaced">which the English say</hi> <seg type="recension">(<hi rend="spaced">call</hi>)</seg> <hi rend="italic">ægylde</hi>.

passages.text: Quicunque uiolauerit ordinem, <hi rend="bold">sicut</hi><ptr n="7" target="IICn_49.lnote.oe.7-3"/><hi rend="bold"> est aut</hi><ptr n="8" target="IICn_49.lnote.oe.8-2"/><hi rend="bold"> monachum aut presbyterum aut aliquem ordinatum uerberauerit aut aliquid huiusmodi fecerit,</hi> hęc<ptr n="9" target="IICn_49.lnote.oe.9"/> ita emendet secundum modum<ptr n="10" target="IICn_49.lnote.oe.10"/> <hi rend="spaced">ordinis</hi><ptr n="11" target="IICn_49.lnote.oe.11"/><hi rend="spaced"> patientis</hi>: aut secundum prętium, id est þere<ptr n="12" target="IICn_49.lnote.oe.12"/><ptr n="13" target="IICn_49.lnote.oe.13"/>, aut secundum forisfacturam<ptr n="13" target="IICn_49.lnote.oe.13"/> aut secundum<ptr n="14" target="IICn_49.lnote.oe.14"/> omnia quę habet <hi rend="spaced">malefactor</hi>.

notes.en: scilicet instead of s. est S

notes.de: uel p. <hi rend="italic">über</hi> ord. <hi rend="italic">H;</hi> pa. or. <hi rend="italic">Di;</hi> et p. <hi rend="italic">Cb; fehlt Lb S</hi>
notes.en: uel p. above ord. H; pa. or. Di; et p. Cb; lacking in Lb S

passages.en: Whoever violates holy orders, <hi rend="bold">as when he beats either a monk or a priest or anyone in orders or does anything of this kind,</hi> let him make amends for these things thus according to the measure of <hi rend="spaced">the order of the injured party</hi>: either according to the price, that is <hi rend="italic">þere</hi>, or according to the forfeiture, or according to all that the <hi rend="spaced">wrongdoer</hi> has.

passages.text: Si<ptr n="15" target="IICn_50-1.lnote.oe.15"/> coniugium quis uiolauerit, <hi rend="bold">uidelicet iacendo sub coniuge sua,</hi> et<ptr n="16" target="IICn_50-1.lnote.oe.16"/> fornicatus fuerit cum <hi rend="spaced">alia femina</hi> uel, quod peius est, cum alterius<ptr n="17" target="IICn_50-1.lnote.oe.17"/> coniugata, faciat pęnitentiam <hi rend="bold">secundum librum pęnitentialem.</hi><ptr n="18" target="IICn_50-1.lnote.oe.18"/>

notes.de: Qui c. uiol. <hi rend="italic">H Lb S</hi>
notes.en: Qui c. uiol. H Lb S

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">so S; fehlt H Di Cb</hi>
notes.en: thus S; lacking in H Di Cb

passages.en: If anyone violates marriage, <hi rend="bold">namely while lying under [i.e. bound to] his own wife,</hi> and fornicates with <hi rend="spaced">another woman</hi> or, what is worse, with another man's wife, let him do penance <hi rend="bold">according to the penitential book.</hi>

passages.text: [52] Uidua<ptr n="21" target="IICn_52.lnote.oe.21"/> <hi rend="spaced">etiam</hi><ptr n="22" target="IICn_52.lnote.oe.22"/>, si ui rapta fuerit, et cum ea coitus factus sit, <hi rend="bold">simili</hi> prętio persoluatur.

notes.de: autem, si r. f. uí <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: autem, si r. f. uí Cb

passages.en: [52] A widow <hi rend="spaced">also</hi>, if she is carried off by force, and intercourse has been had with her, let it be paid for with a <hi rend="bold">like</hi> price.

passages.text: [52, 1] Si quis uirginem ui rapuerit et cum ea coierit, reddat eam<ptr n="19" target="IICn_52-1.lnote.oe.19"/> pretio suo, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> be <hi rend="bold">hyre</hi><ptr n="20" target="IICn_52-1.lnote.oe.20-2"/> þere.
passages.en: [52, 1] If anyone carries off a virgin by force and lies with her, let him pay for her with her price, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> be <hi rend="bold">hyre</hi> <hi rend="italic">þere</hi>.

passages.text: [52, 1] Si quis uirginem ui rapuerit et cum ea coierit, reddat eam<ptr n="19" target="IICn_52-1.lnote.oe.19"/> pretio suo, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> be <hi rend="bold">hyre</hi><ptr n="20" target="IICn_52-1.lnote.oe.20-2"/> þere.
passages.en: [52, 1] If anyone carries off a virgin by force and lies with her, let him pay for her with her price, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> be <hi rend="bold">hyre</hi> <hi rend="italic">þere</hi>.

passages.text: Mulier, quę, uiuente uiro, cum altero uiro adulterata fuerit, et apertum factum sit, fiat sibi ipsi ad opprobrium seculi, et uir eius legalis habeat omnia<ptr n="1" target="IICn_53.lnote.oe.1-3"/> sua; sed illa<ptr n="2" target="IICn_53.lnote.oe.2-3"/> careat naso et auribus.
passages.en: A woman who, while her husband is living, commits adultery with another man, and it is made public, let her become for herself a disgrace before the world, and let her lawful husband have all her property; but let her lose nose and ears.

passages.text: Si autem <hi rend="spaced">negauerit</hi> et pur<hi rend="spaced">gare se uoluerit</hi>, et in <hi rend="bold">iudicio</hi> ceciderit, episcopus <hi rend="spaced">uideat</hi> et districte iudicet<ptr n="3" target="IICn_53-1.lnote.oe.3"/>.
passages.en: But if she <hi rend="spaced">denies</hi> it and <hi rend="spaced">wishes to clear herself</hi>, and fails in the <hi rend="bold">ordeal</hi>, let the bishop <hi rend="spaced">look into it</hi> and judge strictly.

passages.text: Si uir legalem<ptr n="4" target="IICn_54.lnote.oe.4"/> coniugem habens fornicatus cum ancilla sua<ptr n="5" target="IICn_54.lnote.oe.5"/> fuerit, careat ancilla illa et pro semet ipso Deo et hominibus emendet.
passages.en: If a man having a lawful wife fornicates with his slave-woman, let him lose that slave-woman and make amends for himself to God and men.

passages.text: Qui habet legalem coniugem<ptr n="6" target="IICn_54-1.lnote.oe.6"/> et etiam concubinam, nullus presbiter <hi rend="bold">nec aliquis alius</hi> faciat sibi<ptr n="7" target="IICn_54-1.lnote.oe.7"/> aliquod<ptr n="8" target="IICn_54-1.lnote.oe.8"/> seruitium, quod Christiano fieri debet, antequam cessauerit.
passages.en: Whoever has a lawful wife and also a concubine, let no priest <hi rend="bold">nor anyone else</hi> do him any service that ought to be done for a Christian, until he has desisted.

passages.text: Alieni nisi <hi rend="spaced">legale</hi><ptr n="9" target="IICn_55.lnote.oe.9"/> coniugium <hi rend="spaced">custodierint</hi>, expellantur de terra cum substantia et peccatis.<ptr n="10" target="IICn_55.lnote.oe.10"/>
passages.en: If foreigners do not <hi rend="spaced">keep</hi> <hi rend="spaced">lawful</hi> marriage, let them be expelled from the land with their goods and sins.

passages.text: Si apertum<ptr n="11" target="IICn_56.lnote.oe.11"/> mordrum<ptr n="12" target="IICn_56.lnote.oe.12"/> fuerit, ut aliquis <hi rend="spaced">per illud</hi><ptr n="13" target="IICn_56.lnote.oe.13-2"/> occidatur, reddatur parentibus suis.

notes.de: quis a. m. fecerit <hi rend="italic">Lb S</hi>
notes.en: quis a. m. fecerit Lb S
thus H Di; mur. the others

passages.en: If there is open murder, so that someone is killed <hi rend="spaced">by it</hi>, let him be handed over to his kinsmen.

passages.text: Et si <hi rend="spaced">purgatio</hi> euenerit, et in purgatione<ptr n="14" target="IICn_56-1.lnote.oe.14"/> ceciderit, episcopus <hi rend="spaced">uideat et iudicet</hi>.<ptr n="15" target="IICn_56-1.lnote.oe.15"/>
passages.en: And if <hi rend="spaced">a purgation</hi> comes about, and he fails in the purgation, let the bishop <hi rend="spaced">see and judge</hi>.

passages.text: Qui de<ptr n="16" target="IICn_57.lnote.oe.16"/> traditione regis aut domini sui insidiatur, careat omnium bonorum suorum et reus sit mortis, nisi se<ptr n="1" target="IICn_57.lnote.oe.1-4"/> <hi rend="spaced">purgauerit</hi> triplici iudicio.

notes.de: detractioni <hi rend="italic">Cb; verb. aus</hi> detractione <hi rend="italic">H</hi>
notes.en: detractioni Cb; corrected from detractione H

passages.en: Whoever plots treachery against the king or his lord, let him lose all his goods and be guilty of death, unless he <hi rend="spaced">clears</hi> himself by a threefold ordeal.

passages.text: Si quis plegium regis fregerit, emendet<ptr n="2" target="IICn_58.lnote.oe.2-2"/> quinque libris.
passages.en: If anyone breaks the king's pledge, let him make amends with five pounds.

passages.text: Et qui fregerit plegium<ptr n="3" target="IICn_58-1.lnote.oe.3-2"/> archiepiscopi aut reguli, <hi rend="spaced">quem Angli uocant</hi> æðeling, III<ptr n="4" target="IICn_58-1.lnote.oe.4-3"/> libr. emendet<ptr n="5" target="IICn_58-1.lnote.oe.5-3"/>;

notes.en: in the margin Cb; iuditium Di

passages.en: And whoever breaks the pledge of an archbishop or of a prince, <hi rend="spaced">whom the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">æðeling</hi>, let him make amends with III pounds;

passages.text: episcopi<ptr n="6" target="IICn_58-2.lnote.oe.6-2"/> aut<ptr n="7" target="IICn_58-2.lnote.oe.7-2"/> comitis II<ptr n="8" target="IICn_58-2.lnote.oe.8-3"/> libr. emendet.
passages.en: of a bishop or an earl, let him make amends with II pounds.

passages.text: Si quis pugnam fecerit in <seg type="recension">(regali<ptr n="9" target="IICn_59.lnote.oe.9-3"/>)</seg> aula regis, careat uita, nisi ei<ptr n="10" target="IICn_59.lnote.oe.10-3"/> rex parcere uoluerit<ptr n="11" target="IICn_59.lnote.oe.11-3"/>.<ptr n="*" target="IICn_59.lnote.oe.star"/> . . .

notes.de: a. regis <hi rend="italic">Cb;</hi> regali a. <hi rend="italic">H Di</hi>
notes.en: a. regis Cb; regali a. H Di

passages.en: If anyone fights in the <seg type="recension">(royal)</seg> hall of the king, let him lose his life, unless the king wishes to spare him. . . .

passages.text: <ptr n="*" target="Af_15.lnote.incn.star"/>. . . . Qui ante archiepiscopum pugnauerit<ptr n="1" target="Af_15.lnote.incn.1"/> aut arma<ptr n="2" target="Af_15.lnote.incn.2"/> extraxerit, <hi rend="bold">quadraginta</hi> solidos emendet; <hi rend="spaced">et</hi><ptr n="3" target="Af_15.lnote.incn.3"/> qui hoc<ptr n="4" target="Af_15.lnote.incn.4"/> ante episcopum uel comitem <hi rend="spaced">fecerit</hi>, <hi rend="bold">uiginti</hi> sol. emendet.<ptr n="5" target="Af_15.lnote.incn.5"/>

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">Vgl.</hi> Transactions R. Historical Soc., N.S. VII (1893), 77. — <hi rend="italic">Hss.:</hi> H (<hi rend="italic">Textus Roffensis</hi>) <hi rend="italic">um</hi> 1140; Rl (<hi rend="italic">Oxford, Bodley Rawlinson C</hi> 641) <hi rend="italic">um</hi> 1200; T (<hi rend="italic">Titus A</hi> 27) <hi rend="italic">um</hi> 1225; Cb (<hi rend="italic">Paris, Bibl. nat., Latin</hi> 4771, <hi rend="italic">einst Colbert</hi>) <hi rend="italic">um</hi> 1160; Di (<hi rend="italic">Oxford, Bodley Digby</hi> 13) <hi rend="italic">um</hi> 1170; Lb (<hi rend="italic">Lambeth</hi> 118) <hi rend="italic">um</hi> 1200; S (<hi rend="italic">British Mus. Harley</hi> 746) <hi rend="italic">um</hi> 1300; Pl (<hi rend="italic">Phillipps</hi> 8078, <hi rend="italic">seit</hi> 1895 <hi rend="italic">bei H. S.
