passages.en: <hi rend="small">The oath of a noble, <hi rend="spaced">whom</hi><hi rend="spaced"> indeed</hi><hi rend="spaced"> the English</hi><hi rend="spaced"> call</hi> <hi rend="italic">tƿelfhende</hi></hi> <seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(man)</hi></seg><hi rend="small">, <hi rend="spaced">ought to stand and</hi> be worth the oath of six villeins, because his price, that is <hi rend="italic">ƿeregeld</hi> [wergeld], is [that] of six villeins.</hi>

passages.text: <ptr n="36" target="InCn_III-45.lnote.oe.36"/><hi rend="small">Sacramentum presbiteri</hi> regulariter<ptr n="l" target="InCn_III-45.lnote.oe.l"/> <hi rend="small">uiuentis tantundem ualet </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(scilicet</hi><ptr n="37" target="InCn_III-45.lnote.oe.37"/><hi rend="small">)</hi></seg><hi rend="small"> sicut liberalis hominis, propter septem ęcclesiasticos ordines.</hi>

notes.en: The author frequently favours clerical celibacy

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">aus H Rl T; fehlt besser Cb</hi>
notes.en: from H Rl T; better omitted, as in Cb

passages.en: <hi rend="small">The oath of a priest</hi> regularly [by a rule] <hi rend="small">living is worth just as much </hi><seg type="recension"><hi rend="small">(namely)</hi></seg><hi rend="small"> as [that] of a noble, on account of the seven ecclesiastical orders.</hi>

passages.text: Septem <hi rend="spaced">enim</hi> dona<ptr n="1" target="Had_1.lnote.oe.1"/> sunt Spiritus sancti; et septies <hi rend="spaced">presbiteri et alii serui Dei in</hi> <hi rend="spaced">ęcclesiis</hi> debent cotidie Deum<ptr n="2" target="Had_1.lnote.oe.2"/> laudare et pro populo<ptr n="3" target="Had_1.lnote.oe.3"/> Christiano iugiter interuenire.
passages.en: <hi rend="spaced">For</hi> there are seven gifts of the Holy Spirit; and seven times daily <hi rend="spaced">priests and other servants of God in</hi> <hi rend="spaced">churches</hi> ought to praise God and continually intercede for the Christian people.

passages.text: Et propterea quisquis talibus nocere <hi rend="spaced">cupit aut fecit, oportet</hi> eum septupla emendatione illud emendare.
passages.en: And therefore whoever <hi rend="spaced">desires or has done</hi> harm to such, <hi rend="spaced">it is necessary</hi> that he make amends for it with sevenfold compensation.

passages.text: [45, 2] [2—8] Et si <hi rend="spaced">aliquis presbiterum occiderit, excepto eius</hi> iusto prętio, <hi rend="spaced">pro unoquoque ordine</hi> uiginti<ptr n="*" target="Had_2.lnote.oe.star"/> sol.<ptr n="1" target="Had_2.lnote.oe.1"/> emendet, uide<hi rend="spaced">licet ad ordinem ostiarii</hi> uiginti<ptr n="*" target="Had_2.lnote.oe.star"/> sol., item<ptr n="1" target="Had_2.lnote.oe.1"/> <hi rend="spaced">ad exorcistam</hi> <hi rend="spaced">iterum</hi><ptr n="1" target="Had_2.lnote.oe.1"/> uiginti<ptr n="*" target="Had_2.lnote.oe.star"/> sol.<ptr n="1" target="Had_2.lnote.oe.1"/>, et sic <hi rend="spaced">per ordinem</hi>, usque<ptr n="1" target="Had_2.lnote.oe.1"/> <hi rend="spaced">transeat presbiteratum</hi>. [45, 3] <hi rend="spaced">Istę septem librę pro septem ordinibus erunt extra prętium quod dicitur</hi> þeregeld.
passages.en: [45, 2] [2—8] And if <hi rend="spaced">anyone kills a priest, besides his</hi> just price, he shall compensate <hi rend="spaced">for each order</hi> twenty shillings, <hi rend="spaced">namely for the order of doorkeeper</hi> twenty shillings, likewise <hi rend="spaced">for the exorcist</hi> <hi rend="spaced">again</hi> twenty shillings, and so <hi rend="spaced">through the orders</hi>, until <hi rend="spaced">it passes the priesthood</hi>. [45, 3] <hi rend="spaced">These seven pounds for the seven orders will be outside the price which is called</hi> <hi rend="italic">þeregeld</hi>.

passages.text: <ptr n="*" target="Had_9-1.lnote.oe.erkl-clause"/>[9, 1] Et erunt <seg type="recension">(iste<ptr n="2" target="Had_9-1.lnote.oe.2"/>)</seg> iuste episcopi <hi rend="bold">et pauperum.</hi>

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">aus Cb; fehlt H Rl T</hi>
notes.en: from Cb; absent in H Rl T

passages.en: [9, 1] And <seg type="recension">(these)</seg> shall justly be the bishop's <hi rend="bold">and the poor's.</hi>

passages.text: <ptr n="m" target="InCn_III-45-4.lnote.oe.m"/>Istę<ptr n="n" target="InCn_III-45-4.lnote.oe.n"/> sunt consuetudines regum inter Anglos:

notes.de: III 45, 4—55 <hi rend="italic">und</hi> 57—59 <hi rend="italic">übersetzt Verf. aus verlorener Angelsächs. Vorlage</hi> (<hi rend="italic">wohl um</hi> 1050—75) <hi rend="italic">laut</hi> bebodenes 47; ƿunderes 59. <hi rend="italic">Das Latein scheint sein eigen laut</hi> alod, bellum III 46; curia 49 <hi rend="italic">und des auch sonst ihm geläufigen</hi> quod Angli dicunt. <hi rend="italic">Die Entwicklung der Kronprärogative steht hier zwischen</hi> Cnut <hi rend="italic">und</hi> Hn. <hi rend="italic">Vgl. jedoch</hi> III 52<sup>l</sup>
notes.en: The author translates III 45, 4—55 and 57—59 from a lost Anglo-Saxon source (probably c. 1050—75), to judge by bebodenes 47; ƿunderes 59. The Latin seems to be his own, to judge by alod, bellum III 46; curia 49 and by quod Angli dicunt, which is familiar to him elsewhere too. The development of the royal prerogative here stands between Cnut and Hn. Cf., however, III 52<sup>l</sup>

notes.de: Istę — Anglos <hi rend="italic">roth H; fehlt, jedoch mit Raum für Rubrik, Rl; vorher § nachgetragen Cb; vgl.</hi> þis syndon cyning[a] gerihta <hi rend="italic">II Cn.</hi> 12
notes.en: Istę — Anglos in red H; missing, though with space left for a rubric, Rl; preceded by § added later Cb; cf. þis syndon cyning[a] gerihta II Cn. 12

passages.en: These are the customs of the kings among the English:

passages.text: Omnes rectitudines<ptr n="38" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.38"/> ciuitatum<ptr n="o" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.o"/> <seg type="recension">(regis<ptr n="39" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.39"/> sunt)</seg>; et pastum<ptr n="p" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.p"/> [suum cum omnibus rebus quę ad illum<ptr n="40" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.40"/> pastum pertinent; carta alodii<ptr n="q" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.q"/> ad ęternam hęreditatem; forisfactura<ptr n="r" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.r"/> alodii; et prętium<ptr n="s" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.s"/> eorum qui habent alodium<ptr n="q" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.q"/>, quando ita profunde forisfaciunt<ptr n="41" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.41"/> se ipsos; forisfactura<ptr n="42" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.42"/> belli, quod<ptr n="43" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.43"/> Angli uocant ferdƿíte<ptr n="t" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.t"/><ptr n="44" target="InCn_III-46.lnote.oe.44"/> in terra omnium suorum;

notes.de: to ælcere byrig .. hæbbe ic mines cynescipes gerihta <hi rend="italic">IV Eg.</hi> 2<hi rend="italic">a</hi>
notes.en: to ælcere byrig .. hæbbe ic mines cynescipes gerihta IV Eg. 2a

notes.de: r. s. <hi rend="italic">von anderer Hand übergeschrieben Cb; fehlt H Rl T</hi>
notes.en: r. s. written above by another hand Cb; missing in H Rl T

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">vgl. Hn</hi> 20, 3; ælc þæra wita þe þa men gewyrcen þe bocland habban <hi rend="italic">I Atr.</hi> 1, 14
notes.en: cf. Hn 20, 3; ælc þæra wita þe þa men gewyrcen þe bocland habban I Atr. 1, 14

passages.en: All the rights of the cities <seg type="recension">(are the king's)</seg>; and his food-rent [with all the things that pertain to that food-rent; the charter of allod (bookland) for eternal inheritance; the forfeiture of allod; and the price of those who hold allod, when they forfeit themselves so deeply; the forfeiture for war, which the English call <hi rend="italic">ferdƿíte</hi> [fyrd-wite], in the land of all his men;

passages.text: pastio<ptr n="p" target="InCn_III-47.lnote.oe.p"/> proclamati<ptr n="u" target="InCn_III-47.lnote.oe.u"/> exulis, quod Angli dicunt <seg type="recension">(uocant<ptr n="45" target="InCn_III-47.lnote.oe.45"/>)</seg> bebodenes<ptr n="v" target="InCn_III-47.lnote.oe.v"/><ptr n="46" target="InCn_III-47.lnote.oe.46"/> utlage;

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">vgl. oben zu II Cn.</hi> 13, 2 gecydne
notes.en: cf. above on II Cn. 13, 2 gecydne

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">nur</hi> di. <hi rend="italic">H Rl; nur</hi> uo. <hi rend="italic">Cb T</hi>
notes.en: only di. H Rl; only uo. Cb T

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">dieser Genetiv passt grammatisch nicht, weshalb Cb</hi> beboden <hi rend="italic">bessert; in der Quelle hing er von</hi> feorm <hi rend="italic">ab</hi>
notes.en: this genitive does not fit grammatically, which is why Cb corrects it to beboden; in the source it depended on feorm

passages.en: the feeding of a proclaimed exile, which the English say <seg type="recension">(call)</seg> <hi rend="italic">bebodenes utlage</hi> [a commanded outlaw];

passages.text: pastio<ptr n="w" target="InCn_III-48.lnote.oe.w"/> etiam latronum latitantium in siluis<ptr n="x" target="InCn_III-48.lnote.oe.x"/> qui spoliant et occidunt alios <seg type="recension">(<ptr n="1" target="InCn_III-48.lnote.oe.1"/>homines)</seg> — quos Angli uocant fléman<ptr n="2" target="InCn_III-48.lnote.oe.2"/> —; omnis latro extra<ptr n="a" target="InCn_III-48.lnote.oe.a"/> proclamatus; uita<ptr n="3" target="InCn_III-48.lnote.oe.3"/> aut prętium publici<ptr n="b" target="InCn_III-48.lnote.oe.b"/> latronis.

notes.de: flymena fyrmðe <hi rend="italic">Hs. G zu II Cn.</hi> 12
notes.en: flymena fyrmðe M S G on II Cn. 12

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">Verf. scheidet vom ausdrücklich Verbannten den freiwillig dem Rechtsverbande Entwichenen und verengt Ags.</hi> flema <hi rend="italic">unrichtig auf letzteren. Vielleicht entsann er sich des Dänischen Namens</hi> Waldgänger <hi rend="italic">für</hi> utlah; <hi rend="italic">Angelsächs. aber heisst</hi> wealdgenga <hi rend="italic">nur</hi> Räuber, <hi rend="italic">nicht</hi> Verbannter <hi rend="italic">juristisch</hi>
notes.en: The author distinguishes the man who has voluntarily withdrawn from the legal community from the one expressly banished, and wrongly narrows Anglo-Saxon flema to the former. Perhaps he remembered the Danish name Waldgänger for utlah; in Anglo-Saxon, however, wealdgenga means only robber, not banished man in the legal sense

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">nur</hi> a. <hi rend="italic">H Rl T; nur</hi> h. <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: only a. H Rl T; only h. Cb

notes.de: utfangene þeof (<hi rend="italic">vgl.</hi> III 49 extra terminos suos) <hi rend="italic">d. h. gefangen ausserhalb des privilegirten Thatorts, im Gegensatz zu</hi> latrones intra terminos proclamati III 58, 1. <hi rend="italic">Der Begriff</hi> furis comprehensio intus et foris <hi rend="italic">kommt schon</hi> 828 <hi rend="italic">vor, das Wort</hi> utfangen[n]e theof <hi rend="italic">seit Anfang</hi> 12. <hi rend="italic">Jhs.; Birch</hi> Cart. Sax. 395. 1277. <hi rend="italic">Vgl. mein</hi> Über Leges Ed. Conf. <hi rend="italic">p.</hi> 98 <hi rend="italic">f.</hi>
notes.en: utfangene þeof (cf. III 49 extra terminos suos), i.e. caught outside the privileged place of the crime, in contrast to latrones intra terminos proclamati III 58, 1. The concept furis comprehensio intus et foris occurs as early as 828, the word utfangen[n]e theof from the beginning of the 12th cent.; Birch Cart. Sax. 395. 1277. Cf. my Über Leges Ed. Conf. p. 98 f.

notes.de: æbære ðeof <hi rend="italic">II Cn.</hi> 26. 82. <hi rend="italic">Nach II Cn.</hi> 26. 64 <hi rend="italic">ist</hi> open þyfð <hi rend="italic">busslos; Wergeld ersetzt die Todesstrafe des handhaften Diebes III As.</hi> 1, 2 <hi rend="italic">f.;</hi> VI 1, 4 <hi rend="italic">f.;</hi> 12, 1 <hi rend="italic">f.</hi>
notes.en: æbære ðeof II Cn. 26. 82. According to II Cn. 26. 64 open þyfð is bootless; wergild replaces the death penalty of the thief caught in the act III As. 1, 2 f.; VI 1, 4 f.; 12, 1 f.

passages.en: also the feeding of robbers hiding in the woods who plunder and kill others <seg type="recension">(men)</seg> — whom the English call <hi rend="italic">fléman</hi> [fugitives] —; every robber proclaimed outside [the law]; the life or the price of a public robber.

passages.text: Inuasio domus uel curię<ptr n="c" target="InCn_III-49.lnote.oe.c"/>, quod dicitur rihthamsócne<ptr n="d" target="InCn_III-49.lnote.oe.d"/><ptr n="4" target="InCn_III-49.lnote.oe.4"/>, si ille qui fecerit proclamatus fuerit extra<ptr n="a" target="InCn_III-49.lnote.oe.a"/> terminos suos, tunc si uenerit ad emendationem, rex illam habebit.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">Verf. übersetzt</hi> hamsocne <hi rend="italic">ebenso zu II Cn.</hi> 12, <hi rend="italic">der wie</hi> II 15, <hi rend="italic">II Em.</hi> 6, <hi rend="italic">IV Atr.</hi> 4 <hi rend="italic">dies zur Kronprärogative zählt</hi>
notes.en: The author translates hamsocne in the same way on II Cn. 12, which, like II 15, II Em. 6, IV Atr. 4, counts it among the royal prerogatives

notes.de: riht-: völlig, wirklich (<hi rend="italic">wie in</hi> rihthanddæda; rihtlicettere), <hi rend="italic">also Gegensatz zur</hi> unworhtre hamsocne III 58
notes.en: riht-: complete, real (as in rihthanddæda; rihtlicettere), thus in contrast to the unworhtre hamsocne III 58

notes.de: utfangene þeof (<hi rend="italic">vgl.</hi> III 49 extra terminos suos) <hi rend="italic">d. h. gefangen ausserhalb des privilegirten Thatorts, im Gegensatz zu</hi> latrones intra terminos proclamati III 58, 1. <hi rend="italic">Der Begriff</hi> furis comprehensio intus et foris <hi rend="italic">kommt schon</hi> 828 <hi rend="italic">vor, das Wort</hi> utfangen[n]e theof <hi rend="italic">seit Anfang</hi> 12. <hi rend="italic">Jhs.; Birch</hi> Cart. Sax. 395. 1277. <hi rend="italic">Vgl. mein</hi> Über Leges Ed. Conf. <hi rend="italic">p.</hi> 98 <hi rend="italic">f.</hi>
notes.en: utfangene þeof (cf. III 49 extra terminos suos), i.e. caught outside the privileged place of the crime, in contrast to latrones intra terminos proclamati III 58, 1. The concept furis comprehensio intus et foris occurs as early as 828, the word utfangen[n]e theof from the beginning of the 12th cent.; Birch Cart. Sax. 395. 1277. Cf. my Über Leges Ed. Conf. p. 98 f.

passages.en: Invasion of a house or court, which is called <hi rend="italic">rihthamsócne</hi> [true hamsocn], if he who has done it has been proclaimed outside his bounds, then, if he comes to make amends, the king shall have it.

passages.text: Fractionem<ptr n="e" target="InCn_III-50.lnote.oe.e"/> etiam pacis, quod dicitur grithbrece<ptr n="5" target="InCn_III-50.lnote.oe.5"/>: si<ptr n="6" target="InCn_III-50.lnote.oe.6"/> pax ex parte regis pręcipitur in comitatu uel in hundredo, qui post<ptr n="7" target="InCn_III-50.lnote.oe.7"/> illam fregerit, regi emendabit.

notes.de: [si] pax ex <hi rend="italic">fehlt Text, am Rande Corrector Cb</hi>
notes.en: [si] pax ex missing in the text, in the margin by the corrector Cb

passages.en: Also breach of the peace, which is called <hi rend="italic">grithbrece</hi> [grith-breach]: if peace is commanded on the king's part in the shire (court) or in the hundred, whoever breaks it after that shall make amends to the king.

passages.text: Emendatio<ptr n="f" target="InCn_III-50-1.lnote.oe.f"/> fracti pontis in uia regia.
passages.en: The amends for a broken bridge on the king's road.

passages.text: In terra omnium secundum antiquam<ptr n="g" target="InCn_III-51.lnote.oe.g"/><ptr n="8" target="InCn_III-51.lnote.oe.8"/> consuetudinem fractę pacis<ptr n="h" target="InCn_III-51.lnote.oe.h"/> ęcclesię emendatio erit communiter<ptr n="i" target="InCn_III-51.lnote.oe.i"/> regis et episcopi.

notes.de: ciricgrið <hi rend="italic">oder</hi> mynstres griðbryce <hi rend="italic">I Cn.</hi> 3, 2
notes.en: ciricgrið or mynstres griðbryce I Cn. 3, 2

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">vgl.</hi> 53. <hi rend="italic">Todtschläger in der Kirche zahlt Wergeld</hi> episcopo et regi <hi rend="italic">Hn</hi> 11, 1<hi rend="italic">a; der König erhält Strafgeld-Antheil bei sonstiger Verletzung des Rechtes der Kirche</hi> EGu. 4; Hn 11, 5; VIII Atr. 8. 15. 36; <hi rend="italic">bei Widerstand gegen Bischofsgebot</hi> EGu. Pr. 2
notes.en: cf. 53. A slayer in a church pays wergild episcopo et regi Hn 11, 1a; the king receives a share of the fine for other infringements of the rights of the Church EGu. 4; Hn 11, 5; VIII Atr. 8. 15. 36; for resistance to a bishop’s command EGu. Pr. 2

passages.en: In the land of all men, according to ancient custom, the amends for broken peace of the church shall be in common the king's and the bishop's.

passages.text: Et multas alias<ptr n="k" target="InCn_III-51-1.lnote.oe.k"/> consuetudines habet rex, quę sibi conueniunt.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">vielleicht meint Verf. Theile des Inhalts von</hi> Hn 10, 1
notes.en: perhaps the author means parts of the content of Hn 10, 1

passages.en: And the king has many other customs which befit him.

passages.text: <ptr n="l" target="InCn_III-52.lnote.oe.l"/>Qui diuisionem<ptr n="m" target="InCn_III-52.lnote.oe.m"/> habet iuxta terram regis, claudat<ptr n="n" target="InCn_III-52.lnote.oe.n"/> contra regem aut custodiat aut dilectione aut prętio adquirat, si uoluerit aliquam <seg type="recension">(commoditatem<ptr n="9" target="InCn_III-52.lnote.oe.9"/>)</seg> in terra illa aisiam<ptr n="o" target="InCn_III-52.lnote.oe.o"/> habere.

notes.de: III 52 <hi rend="italic">gehört vielleicht auch inhaltlich dem Verf.: er schilt Übergriffe königlicher Beamter auch</hi> II 69, 1, <hi rend="italic">o. S.</hi> 357
notes.en: III 52 perhaps belongs to the author in its content as well: he also censures encroachments by royal officials in II 69, 1, above p. 357

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">Verf. warnt nicht vor Schaden durch eindringendes Vieh</hi> (Ine 40. 42, <hi rend="italic">welche Gefahr jeder Nachbar bot</hi>), <hi rend="italic">noch denkt er an Servitut auf Königsboden, sondern warnt vor der Chicane des mit Processvorrecht privilegirten Fiscalvogts, der wegen Schädigung der Königsdomäne an Ernte, Vieh, Wald oder Wild oder wegen Überfang klagen mochte gegen den nachbarlichen Grundbesitzer, wenn dieser nicht sein Gut deutlich einhegte</hi>
notes.en: The author is not warning against damage from intruding cattle (Ine 40. 42, a danger that any neighbour posed), nor is he thinking of a servitude on royal land; rather he warns against the chicanery of the fiscal reeve, privileged with procedural prerogative, who might sue the neighbouring landowner for damage to the royal demesne in crops, cattle, woodland or game, or for encroachment, if the latter did not clearly fence in his estate

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">so H Rl statt Cb T's</hi> aisiam, <hi rend="italic">das fehlt;</hi> co. <hi rend="italic">fehlt Cb T</hi> [<hi rend="italic">offenbar nachträgliche Latinisirung</hi>]
notes.en: thus H Rl instead of Cb T’s aisiam, which is missing; co. missing in Cb T [evidently a later Latinization]

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">altfranz.</hi> aise, <hi rend="italic">mittelengl.</hi> eise: ‘<hi rend="italic">behagliche Ruhe</hi>’
notes.en: Old French aise, Middle English eise: ‘comfortable rest’

passages.en: Whoever has a boundary next to the king's land, let him fence against the king or keep watch, or acquire it by goodwill or by price, if he wishes to have any <seg type="recension">(advantage)</seg> easement in that land.

passages.text: Antiqua<ptr n="g" target="InCn_III-53.lnote.oe.g"/> consuetudo fuit, ut omnis ęcclesiastica et<ptr n="q" target="InCn_III-53.lnote.oe.q"/> secularis emendatio communis erat regi et episcopo.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">meint Verf.:</hi> gemischt kirchlich-staatlich <hi rend="italic">wie</hi> III 51, <hi rend="italic">bei Heidenthum</hi> EGu. Pr. 2, <hi rend="italic">Incest</hi> EGu. 4, <hi rend="italic">bei Zehntweigerung</hi> II Eg. 3, 1 (<hi rend="italic">daraus</hi> VIII Atr. 8. 15. 36), adulterium Hn 11, 5? <hi rend="italic">Jedenfalls ist</hi> omnis <hi rend="italic">übertrieben wie</hi> omnia III 57
notes.en: does the author mean mixed ecclesiastical and secular, as in III 51, in cases of heathenism EGu. Pr. 2, incest EGu. 4, refusal of tithe II Eg. 3, 1 (whence VIII Atr. 8. 15. 36), adulterium Hn 11, 5? In any case omnis is an exaggeration, like omnia III 57

passages.en: It was an ancient custom that every ecclesiastical and secular amends was common to the king and the bishop.

passages.text: Hoc etiam debet quisque scire, quia<ptr n="r" target="InCn_III-54.lnote.oe.r"/>, si<ptr n="10" target="InCn_III-54.lnote.oe.10"/> pro aliqua forisfactura, quę ad Deum<ptr n="11" target="InCn_III-54.lnote.oe.11"/> pertineat<ptr n="12" target="InCn_III-54.lnote.oe.12"/>, accipitur<ptr n="13" target="InCn_III-54.lnote.oe.13"/> pecunia ab episcopo uel ab aliquo alio, episcopus debet eandem pecuniam distribuere ęcclesiis et pauperibus<ptr n="s" target="InCn_III-54.lnote.oe.s"/>.

notes.de: gif for godbotan feohbot ariseð, .. to þearfena hyþþe ⁊ to cyricbote; VI Atr. 51; <hi rend="italic">vgl.</hi> Can. Edgari 55. <hi rend="italic">Auch</hi> III 45, 3 <hi rend="italic">setzt Verf.</hi> pauperum <hi rend="italic">zu</hi> Had 9, 1
notes.en: gif for godbotan feohbot ariseð, .. to þearfena hyþþe ⁊ to cyricbote; VI Atr. 51; cf. Can. Edgari 55. In III 45, 3 too the author adds pauperum to Had 9, 1

passages.en: This too each man ought to know, that, if for any forfeiture which pertains to God money is taken by the bishop or by any other, the bishop ought to distribute that same money to churches and to the poor.

passages.text: Comitis<ptr n="t" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.t"/> rectitudines secundum Anglos istę sunt communes cum rege: tertius denarius in uillis<ptr n="u" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.u"/> ubi mercatum conuenerit<ptr n="14" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.14"/> et in<ptr n="v" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.v"/> castigatione latronum<ptr n="w" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.w"/>; et comitales<ptr n="x" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.x"/> uillas quę pertinent<ptr n="15" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.15"/> ad comitatum eius; et consuetudines liberalium<ptr n="a" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.a"/> hominum duppliciter<ptr n="b" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.b"/> omnes habere, uidelicet duplicem<ptr n="1" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.1"/> mundam<ptr n="c" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.c"/>, duplicem manbote<ptr n="d" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.d"/> et forisfacturam<ptr n="e" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.e"/> <seg type="recension">(duplicem<ptr n="2" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.2"/>)</seg>; duplex<ptr n="f" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.f"/> etiam habere<ptr n="3" target="InCn_III-55.lnote.oe.3"/> debet prętium, id est þere.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">obwohl nicht unter Rubrik</hi> 45, 4 <hi rend="italic">gehörig, stammt</hi> 55 <hi rend="italic">wohl aus derselben Quelle</hi>
notes.en: although it does not belong under the rubric 45, 4, 55 probably comes from the same source

notes.de: Domesday <hi rend="italic">giebt dem Grafen den</hi> tertius denarius redditus burgi <hi rend="italic">von Chester, Chichester, Derby, Dover, Exeter, Fordwich, Huntingdon, Ipswich, Lewes, Lincoln, Shrewsbury, Stafford; Round</hi> Geoffrey of Mandeville 287
notes.en: Domesday gives the earl the tertius denarius redditus burgi of Chester, Chichester, Derby, Dover, Exeter, Fordwich, Huntingdon, Ipswich, Lewes, Lincoln, Shrewsbury, Stafford; Round Geoffrey of Mandeville 287

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">den</hi> tertius denarius placitorum comitatus <hi rend="italic">giebt dem Grafen</hi> Domesday <hi rend="italic">für York-, Lincoln-, Nottingham- und Derbyshire. Im</hi> 12. <hi rend="italic">Jh. verlieh ihn Königsurkunde, keineswegs in allen Grafschaften:</hi> Comes .. tertiam portionem eorum que de placitis proueniunt in comitatu quolibet percipit; ... set hii tantum, .. quibus regum munificentia ... decernit; [<hi rend="italic">Ric. fil. Nigelli</hi>] Dial. de scaccario I 17 <hi rend="italic">um</hi> 1178; <hi rend="italic">vgl. Round</hi> 293
notes.en: Domesday gives the earl the tertius denarius placitorum comitatus for York-, Lincoln-, Nottingham- and Derbyshire. In the 12th cent. it was granted by royal charter, by no means in all counties: Comes .. tertiam portionem eorum que de placitis proueniunt in comitatu quolibet percipit; ... set hii tantum, .. quibus regum munificentia ... decernit; [<hi rend="italic">Ric. fil. Nigelli</hi>] Dial. de scaccario I 17 c. 1178; cf. <hi rend="italic">Round</hi> 293

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">Quelle:</hi> on þeofa steore; <hi rend="italic">vgl.</hi> III 58, 1
notes.en: Source: on þeofa steore; cf. III 58, 1

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">über</hi> Manors des Grafenthums <hi rend="italic">vgl. Maitland</hi> Domesday 168; <hi rend="italic">Round</hi> Feudal Engl. 115. <hi rend="italic">Amtsland erkennt unter</hi> þæs ealdormonnes lond <hi rend="italic">der Grenzen in Urkunden Schmid</hi> Gesetze 560<hi rend="italic">b</hi>; <hi rend="italic">solches wohl meint</hi> I As. Pr.
notes.en: on manors of the earldom cf. <hi rend="italic">Maitland</hi> Domesday 168; <hi rend="italic">Round</hi> Feudal Engl. 115. Schmid Gesetze 560b recognizes land attached to the office in the þæs ealdormonnes lond of the boundary clauses in charters; this is probably what I As. Pr. means

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">wohl verallgemeinert aus dem Recht des Grafen in Denalagu, als Kläger vom Verklagten doppelt so viel Bürgen als der Thegn zu fordern</hi> (III Atr. 12), <hi rend="italic">und aus etwa doppeltem Heergewæte</hi> II Cn. 71<hi rend="italic">a</hi>; 1
notes.en: probably generalized from the earl's right in the Danelaw, as plaintiff, to demand from the defendant twice as many sureties as the thegn (III Atr. 12), and from the roughly double heriot II Cn. 71a; 1

notes.de: burgbryce ealdormonnes LX, twelfhyndes XXX scill.; <hi rend="italic">Af</hi> 40
notes.en: burgbryce ealdormonnes LX, twelfhyndes XXX scill.; <hi rend="italic">Af</hi> 40

notes.de: manbote comiti XX sol., baronibus X sol., <hi rend="italic">ECf.</hi> 12, 5; manbot <hi rend="italic">steigert Verf. mit dem Stande des Herrn auch</hi> 56, 2 <hi rend="italic">gegen Hn</hi> 87, 4<hi rend="italic">a</hi>{q}
notes.en: manbote comiti XX sol., baronibus X sol., <hi rend="italic">ECf.</hi> 12, 5; the author also makes manbot rise with the rank of the lord in 56, 2, contrary to <hi rend="italic">Hn</hi> 87, 4a{q}

notes.de: wite <hi rend="italic">im Sinne von</hi> despectus 56, 2 (oferseunes), <hi rend="italic">darunter</hi> fihtwite; <hi rend="italic">vgl. Hn</hi> 69, 1<hi rend="italic">a</hi>. 94, 2<hi rend="italic">c</hi>
notes.en: wite in the sense of despectus 56, 2 (oferseunes), including fihtwite; cf. <hi rend="italic">Hn</hi> 69, 1a. 94, 2c

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">aus Cb; fehlt H Rl T</hi>
notes.en: from Cb; absent in H Rl T

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">ob irgendwo richtig? Den Ealdorman bewerthet wie vier Thegnas</hi> Norðleod 3
notes.en: correct anywhere? Norðleod 3 values the ealdorman as equal to four thegns

passages.en: The earl's rights according to the English, these are common with the king: the third penny in towns where a market has come together and in the punishment of thieves; and the comital towns which pertain to his shire; and to have all the customs of free men of rank (thegns) doubly, namely double <hi rend="italic">mund</hi> [protection], double <hi rend="italic">manbote</hi> [man-amends] and <seg type="recension">(double)</seg> forfeiture; he must also have a double price, that is <hi rend="italic">þere</hi> [wer].

passages.text: <hi rend="small">In lege Cantia</hi><ptr n="4" target="InCn_III-56.lnote.oe.4"/><hi rend="small"> Ęcclesia Christi et rex et archiepiscopus habent similem et ęque carum despectum, </hi><hi rend="spaced"><hi rend="small">quod Angli dicunt</hi></hi><hi rend="small"> mundbrece</hi><ptr n="5" target="InCn_III-56.lnote.oe.5"/><hi rend="small">.</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="small">In the law of Kent Christ Church and the king and the archbishop have a like and equally dear contempt-fine, </hi><hi rend="spaced"><hi rend="small">which the English call</hi></hi><hi rend="small"> <hi rend="italic">mundbrece</hi> [breach of protection].</hi>

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Et in illa lege pecunia archiepiscopi undecies <hi rend="spaced">reddetur</hi>, pecunia autem</hi><ptr n="6" target="InCn_III-56-1.lnote.oe.6"/><hi rend="small"> regis <hi rend="spaced">non</hi> reddetur <hi rend="spaced">nisi</hi> nouies.</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="small">And in that law the archbishop's property <hi rend="spaced">shall be repaid</hi> elevenfold, but the king's property shall <hi rend="spaced">not</hi> be repaid <hi rend="spaced">except</hi> ninefold.</hi>

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Ali[a]s</hi><ptr n="7" target="InCn_III-56-2.lnote.oe.7"/><hi rend="small"> archiepiscopus et <hi rend="spaced">filius regis</hi></hi><ptr n="g" target="InCn_III-56-2.lnote.oe.g"/><hi rend="small"> <hi rend="spaced">de legali coniuge habent similem secularem rectitudinem</hi></hi> in multis rebus, <hi rend="small">hoc est in despectu</hi><ptr n="h" target="InCn_III-56-2.lnote.oe.h"/><hi rend="small">,</hi> in<ptr n="8" target="InCn_III-56-2.lnote.oe.8"/> emendatione hominis occisi, quod dicitur manbote<ptr n="d" target="InCn_III-56-2.lnote.oe.d"/>, et in multis aliis diuersis<ptr n="9" target="InCn_III-56-2.lnote.oe.9"/> rebus, id est þere prętio<ptr n="i" target="InCn_III-56-2.lnote.oe.i"/> reddendo et forisfactura<seg type="recension">(m)</seg><ptr n="k" target="InCn_III-56-2.lnote.oe.k"/><ptr n="10" target="InCn_III-56-2.lnote.oe.10"/>, utroque<ptr n="11" target="InCn_III-56-2.lnote.oe.11"/> ęque magnum et carum.

notes.de: alius <hi rend="italic">H Rl Cb;</hi> alterius <hi rend="italic">T; gebessert Kolderup</hi> [<hi rend="italic">aus</hi> elles?]
notes.en: alius <hi rend="italic">H Rl Cb;</hi> alterius <hi rend="italic">T</hi>; emended by Kolderup [from elles?]

notes.de: æþeling <hi rend="italic">stand in des Verfassers Quelle. Er verengt den Begriff (zum Unterschiede von Heinrichs I. Bastarden und im Hinblick auf den Thronfolger</hi> Wilhelm Æþeling) <hi rend="italic">zu sehr; denn</hi> Eadgar Æþeling, <hi rend="italic">der Bruder der Königin, war kein Königssohn</hi>
notes.en: æþeling stood in the author's source. He narrows the concept too much (to distinguish it from Henry I's bastards and with an eye to the heir to the throne, William Æþeling); for Eadgar Æþeling, the queen's brother, was no king's son

notes.de: manbote comiti XX sol., baronibus X sol., <hi rend="italic">ECf.</hi> 12, 5; manbot <hi rend="italic">steigert Verf. mit dem Stande des Herrn auch</hi> 56, 2 <hi rend="italic">gegen Hn</hi> 87, 4<hi rend="italic">a</hi>{q}
notes.en: manbote comiti XX sol., baronibus X sol., <hi rend="italic">ECf.</hi> 12, 5; the author also makes manbot rise with the rank of the lord in 56, 2, contrary to <hi rend="italic">Hn</hi> 87, 4a{q}

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">verbessert aus</hi> r. d. <hi rend="italic">Rl Cb</hi>
notes.en: corrected from r. d. <hi rend="italic">Rl Cb</hi>

notes.de: arcebiscopes ⁊ æþelinges wergild is . . <hi rend="italic">Norðleod</hi> 2; <hi rend="italic">die Benutzung dieses Stückes ist wahrscheinlich, weil</hi> Mirce, Að, Had <hi rend="italic">benutzt sind, mit denen es stets zusammen erscheint; vgl. o. S.</hi> 613{h}
notes.en: arcebiscopes ⁊ æþelinges wergild is . . <hi rend="italic">Norðleod</hi> 2; the use of this piece is probable, because Mirce, Að, Had have been used, with which it always appears together; cf. above p. 613{h}

notes.de: beforan æðelinge oððe arcebiscpe gefeoht . . <hi rend="italic">Grið</hi> 12; <hi rend="italic">vgl.</hi> III 55{e}
notes.en: beforan æðelinge oððe arcebiscpe gefeoht . . <hi rend="italic">Grið</hi> 12; cf. III 55{e}

passages.en: <hi rend="small">Other[wise] the archbishop and the <hi rend="spaced">king's son</hi> <hi rend="spaced">by a lawful wife have a like secular right</hi></hi> in many things, <hi rend="small">that is in the contempt-fine,</hi> in the amends for a slain man, which is called <hi rend="italic">manbote</hi> [man-amends], and in many other different things, that is in paying the <hi rend="italic">þere</hi> [wer] price and the forfeiture<seg type="recension">(m)</seg>, both equally great and dear.

passages.text: Episcopus<ptr n="l" target="InCn_III-57.lnote.oe.l"/> et comes habent<ptr n="12" target="InCn_III-57.lnote.oe.12"/> multas seculares leges ęquales; etiam<ptr n="13" target="InCn_III-57.lnote.oe.13"/> omnia<ptr n="m" target="InCn_III-57.lnote.oe.m"/><ptr n="14" target="InCn_III-57.lnote.oe.14"/> olim<ptr n="n" target="InCn_III-57.lnote.oe.n"/> idem habuerunt propter excellentiam ordinis.

notes.de: biscopes ⁊ ealdormannes wergild . . <hi rend="italic">Norðleod</hi> 3; mundbrice . . biscpæs ⁊ ealdormannes; . . . gefeoht . . beforan . . biscpe oððe ealdormen <hi rend="italic">Grið</hi> 11. 12; æt eorles ⁊ biscopes . . spæce lecge man <hi rend="italic">III Atr.</hi> 12
notes.en: biscopes ⁊ ealdormannes wergild . . <hi rend="italic">Norðleod</hi> 3; mundbrice . . biscpæs ⁊ ealdormannes; . . . gefeoht . . beforan . . biscpe oððe ealdormen <hi rend="italic">Grið</hi> 11. 12; æt eorles ⁊ biscopes . . spæce lecge man <hi rend="italic">III Atr.</hi> 12

notes.de: &iam, <hi rend="italic">dazu vor</hi> iam <hi rend="italic">übergeschr.</hi> et <hi rend="italic">Cb;</hi> et anima <hi rend="italic">statt</hi> e. o. <hi rend="italic">T</hi>
notes.en: &iam, with et written above before iam <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>; et anima instead of e. o. <hi rend="italic">T</hi>

passages.en: The bishop and the earl have many equal secular laws; indeed formerly they had all the same, on account of the excellence of their order.

passages.text: Episcopi<ptr n="o" target="InCn_III-58.lnote.oe.o"/> inprimis ęcclesiasticam <seg type="recension">(habeant<ptr n="15" target="InCn_III-58.lnote.oe.15"/>)</seg> correctionem et Christianam dominationem super omnes, quos <hi rend="small">debent</hi><ptr n="p" target="InCn_III-58.lnote.oe.p"/><hi rend="small"> docere et ante iudicium Dei eos ducere et</hi> pręire.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">auch</hi> 58 <hi rend="italic">f. floss aus Angelsächs. Vorlage laut Angelsächs. Wörter, unkanonistischer Form und des <hi rend="spaced">vor</hi></hi> Wl ep. <hi rend="italic">zu datirenden Inhalts</hi>
notes.en: 58 f. too derived from an Anglo-Saxon original, as shown by the Anglo-Saxon words, the uncanonistic form and the content, which is to be dated <hi rend="italic">before</hi> Wl ep.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">in anderer Tinte übergeschr. Cb; fehlt H Rl T</hi>
notes.en: written above in different ink <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>; missing in <hi rend="italic">H Rl T</hi>

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">hier aus</hi> Cnut <hi rend="italic">Benutztes liess Verf. o. S.</hi> 367{14} <hi rend="italic">fort</hi>
notes.en: what is used here from Cnut the author omitted above p. 367{14}

passages.en: Bishops above all <seg type="recension">(should have)</seg> ecclesiastical correction and Christian lordship over all, whom they <hi rend="small">ought to teach and to lead before the judgment of God and</hi> to go before.

passages.text: In multis tamen locis secundum<ptr n="q" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.q"/> iusticiam in sua propria<ptr n="r" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.r"/> terra et in suis<ptr n="r" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.r"/> uillis debent habere constitutionem hundredi<ptr n="s" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.s"/>, quod Angli dicunt<ptr n="t" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.t"/> hundrædsétene<ptr n="16" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.16"/>; et prętium latronum<ptr n="u" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.u"/> infra<ptr n="17" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.17"/> terminos eorum <seg type="recension">(proclamatorum<ptr n="18" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.18"/>)</seg>; et infectam<ptr n="v" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.v"/> inuasionem, quod Angli dicunt <seg type="recension">(<ptr n="19" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.19"/>dicitur)</seg> unƿorhtre<ptr n="v" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.v"/><ptr n="20" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.20"/> hamsocne; et toll<ptr n="21" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.21"/> ⁊ team; et correctionem<ptr n="w" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.w"/> latronum, quousque<ptr n="x" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.x"/> sit<ptr n="22" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.22"/> condemnatus<ptr n="23" target="InCn_III-58-1.lnote.oe.23"/> ad mortem;

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">auf des Bisthums Eigengütern; vgl. Hn</hi> 20, 2: episcopi . . in terris proprii potentatus . . habent tol et theam et infongenþeaf
notes.en: on the bishopric's own estates; cf. <hi rend="italic">Hn</hi> 20, 2: episcopi . . in terris proprii potentatus . . habent tol et theam et infongenþeaf

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">manches Bisthum besass ganze Hundertschaften, so Worcester. Doch heisst</hi> hundred <hi rend="italic">auch jedes andere weltliche Gericht; o. S.</hi> 485{d}
notes.en: many a bishopric possessed whole hundreds, Worcester for instance. But hundred also denotes any other secular court; above p. 485{d}

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">ein vor</hi> 1137 <hi rend="italic">gefälschtes Privileg Eadgars giebt Glastonbury</hi> hundredsetene; <hi rend="italic">Birch</hi> Cart. Sax. 1277
notes.en: a privilege of Eadgar forged before 1137 grants Glastonbury hundredsetene; <hi rend="italic">Birch</hi> Cart. Sax. 1277

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">aus Cb T; fehlt H Rl</hi>
notes.en: from <hi rend="italic">Cb T</hi>; missing in <hi rend="italic">H Rl</hi>

notes.de: unvollendet, <hi rend="italic">wie in II Cn.</hi> 61 <hi rend="italic">im Gegensatz zu der dem König gehörigen</hi> rihthamsocne III 49. Unworhtre <hi rend="italic">ist Genetiv; er hing im Original vielleicht ab von</hi> beo weorð
notes.en: unfinished, as in II Cn. 61, in contrast to the rihthamsocne belonging to the king III 49. Unworhtre is a genitive; in the original it perhaps depended on beo weorð

notes.de: A. d-t <hi rend="italic">H Rl;</hi> dicitur <hi rend="italic">ohne</hi> A. <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: A. d-t <hi rend="italic">H Rl;</hi> dicitur without A. <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">Bischof Theodred</hi> 926—51 (<hi rend="italic">Will. Malm.</hi> Pont. II 73) <hi rend="italic">und Dunstan liessen hinrichten; Lanfranc führte in England den Canon von Toledo ein</hi> (<hi rend="italic">nach Burns</hi> I 219 <hi rend="italic">aus Gibson</hi> Instit. 125); <hi rend="italic">später</hi> episcopi debent interesse iudiciis curiae regis, usque perueniatur ad mortem; <hi rend="italic">Constitut. Clarendon.</hi> 11; <hi rend="italic">festländische Kanonistik hierüber seit</hi> 12. <hi rend="italic">Jh. bei Dove</hi> Iurisdict. eccles. progr. 116
notes.en: Bishop Theodred 926—51 (<hi rend="italic">Will. Malm.</hi> Pont. II 73) and Dunstan had men executed; Lanfranc introduced the canon of Toledo into England (according to <hi rend="italic">Burns</hi> I 219, from <hi rend="italic">Gibson</hi> Instit. 125); later episcopi debent interesse iudiciis curiae regis, usque perueniatur ad mortem; <hi rend="italic">Constitut. Clarendon.</hi> 11; Continental canon law on this point since the 12th cent. in <hi rend="italic">Dove</hi> Iurisdict. eccles. progr. 116

passages.en: In many places, however, according to justice, in their own land and in their towns they ought to have the setting of the hundred, which the English call <hi rend="italic">hundrædsétene</hi> [hundred-session]; and the price of thieves <seg type="recension">(proclaimed)</seg> within their bounds; and unaccomplished invasion, which the English call <seg type="recension">(which is called)</seg> <hi rend="italic">unƿorhtre hamsocne</hi> [attempted hamsocn]; and <hi rend="italic">toll ⁊ team</hi>; and the correction of thieves, until he is condemned to death;

passages.text: sic<ptr n="24" target="InCn_III-59.lnote.oe.24"/> etiam monetarios<ptr n="y" target="InCn_III-59.lnote.oe.y"/> et púndæres<ptr n="25" target="InCn_III-59.lnote.oe.25"/> uel<ptr n="26" target="InCn_III-59.lnote.oe.26"/> ponderatores; et loca<ptr n="z" target="InCn_III-59.lnote.oe.z"/> iudiciorum ferri aut aquę; proprias mensuras et pondera<ptr n="y" target="InCn_III-59.lnote.oe.y"/>; et multas uarias consuetudines, quas statuerunt qúi Dei<ptr n="27" target="InCn_III-59.lnote.oe.27"/> honorem <seg type="recension">(et<ptr n="2" target="InCn_III-59.lnote.oe.2"/> iustitiam)</seg> amauerunt.

notes.de: Jurisdiction über öffentliche Münzer und Wäger. <hi rend="italic">Laut königlicher Gesetze falsch verallgemeinert aus den an einigen Orten verwirklichten Ansätzen zu hierarchischer Beschlagnahme der Münz-, Gewicht- und Maass-Verwaltung: Synode a.</hi> 786; II As. 14; Episc. 6. <hi rend="italic">Eigenes Münzgewicht besass Graf Eustach in Hertfordshire:</hi> terra . . ualet 22 libras de albis denariis ad pensum huius comitis; <hi rend="italic">Domesday</hi> I 137, 2
notes.en: Jurisdiction over public moneyers and weighers. As royal laws show, wrongly generalized from the beginnings, realized in some places, of the hierarchy's appropriation of the administration of coinage, weights and measures: Synod a. 786; II As. 14; Episc. 6. Count Eustace possessed his own coin-weight in Hertfordshire: terra . . ualet 22 libras de albis denariis ad pensum huius comitis; <hi rend="italic">Domesday</hi> I 137, 2

notes.de: et l. i. f. aut aq. (<hi rend="italic">fehlt T</hi>) uel po. aque pro. <hi rend="italic">Cb T</hi>
notes.en: et l. i. f. aut aq. (missing in <hi rend="italic">T</hi>) uel po. aque pro. <hi rend="italic">Cb T</hi>

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">Feuerordal geschah in der Kirche; das Gewässer zum Kaltwasserordal war geweiht, unterstand also bischöflicher Mund</hi>
notes.en: The ordeal of fire took place in the church; the water for the cold-water ordeal was consecrated, and thus came under the bishop's protection

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">aus Cb; fehlt H Rl T</hi>
notes.en: from Cb; absent in H Rl T

passages.en: so also moneyers and <hi rend="italic">púndæres</hi> or weighers; and places of the ordeals of iron or water; their own measures and weights; and many various customs, which those established who loved God's honour <seg type="recension">(and justice)</seg>.

passages.text: <ptr n="*" target="Gethyn_1.lnote.oe.erkl-clause"/>[60] <ptr n="1" target="Gethyn_1.lnote.oe.1"/><hi rend="spaced">Antiqua</hi> <hi rend="bold">lex Anglorum</hi> fuit, quod<ptr n="2" target="Gethyn_1.lnote.oe.2-2"/> <hi rend="spaced">gens</hi><ptr n="3" target="Gethyn_1.lnote.oe.3"/> <hi rend="spaced">illorúm</hi><ptr n="a" target="Gethyn_1.lnote.oe.a"/> et consuetudines in honore tenebantur; et <hi rend="bold">per consilium</hi> dabantur <seg type="recension">(uni-<ptr n="4" target="Gethyn_1.lnote.oe.4"/>)</seg> cuique secundum mensuram cuiusque <hi rend="spaced">comiti et uillano</hi>, liberali et <hi rend="bold">subliberali.</hi>

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">aus Cb; fehlt H Rl T</hi>
notes.en: from Cb; missing in H Rl T

passages.en: [60] It was an <hi rend="spaced">ancient</hi> <hi rend="bold">law of the English</hi> that <hi rend="spaced">their</hi> <hi rend="spaced">people</hi> and customs were held in honour; and <hi rend="bold">by counsel</hi> [rights] were given to <seg type="recension">(every)</seg> each according to the measure of each, <hi rend="spaced">to earl and villein</hi>, to the free man of rank (thegn) and to the <hi rend="bold">lesser free man</hi>.

passages.text: [60, 1] Et si uillanus ita creuisset <hi rend="bold">sua probitate,</hi> quod pleniter haberet quinque hídas<ptr n="5" target="Gethyn_2.lnote.oe.5"/> de suo próprio <hi rend="spaced">alodio</hi><ptr n="6" target="Gethyn_2.lnote.oe.6"/> <hi rend="bold">et ęcclesiam propriam</hi> et clocarium<ptr n="7" target="Gethyn_2.lnote.oe.7"/> <hi rend="bold">et coquinam</hi> et portam, sedem et priuatum profectum in aula regis, tunc deinde erat dignus honore liberalitatis<ptr n="8" target="Gethyn_2.lnote.oe.8"/>, <hi rend="spaced">quod Angli dicunt</hi> þegen<hi rend="bold">scipes</hi><ptr n="9" target="Gethyn_2.lnote.oe.9"/> þurðe<ptr n="10" target="Gethyn_2.lnote.oe.10"/>.

notes.de: idas <hi rend="italic">T; verb. aus</hi> idas <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: idas T; corrected from idas Cb

passages.en: [60, 1] And if a villein had so prospered <hi rend="bold">by his own worth</hi> that he fully had five hides of his own <hi rend="spaced">allod</hi> <hi rend="bold">and his own church</hi> and bell-house <hi rend="bold">and kitchen</hi> and gate, a seat and special office in the king's hall, then thenceforth he was worthy of the honour of nobility, <hi rend="spaced">which the English call</hi> <hi rend="italic">þegen<hi rend="bold">scipes</hi> þurðe</hi> [worthy of thegnship].

passages.text: [61] <hi rend="bold">Si</hi> autem liberalis homo, id est þegen<ptr n="9" target="Gethyn_3.lnote.oe.9"/>, <hi rend="spaced">ita profecisset</hi>, ut regi seruisset et <hi rend="spaced">uice sua</hi> equitaret in <hi rend="bold">missiático</hi> regis, is<ptr n="11" target="Gethyn_3.lnote.oe.11"/> talis, si haberet <hi rend="spaced">alium sub sé</hi>, qui ad <hi rend="bold">expeditionem</hi><ptr n="12" target="Gethyn_3.lnote.oe.12"/> regis quinque hidas<ptr n="13" target="Gethyn_3.lnote.oe.13"/> teneret et in aula regis suo<ptr n="14" target="Gethyn_3.lnote.oe.14"/> domino seruisset et ter<ptr n="15" target="Gethyn_3.lnote.oe.15"/> nuntius domini<ptr n="16" target="Gethyn_3.lnote.oe.16"/> sui regem adisset, is<ptr n="11" target="Gethyn_3.lnote.oe.11"/>, <hi rend="spaced">inquam</hi>, talis dehinc <hi rend="spaced">potest</hi> pro domino suo preiurare iuramentum, <hi rend="bold">quod supra</hi><ptr n="b" target="Gethyn_3.lnote.oe.b"/><hi rend="bold"> nominauimus</hi> foraþ<ptr n="17" target="Gethyn_3.lnote.oe.17"/>, <hi rend="bold">in diuersis rebus,</hi> ubicunque opus est.

notes.de: d. s. <hi rend="italic">fehlt hier, aber</hi> reg. a., is i. t. domini sui de. <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: d. s. missing here, but reg. a., is i. t. domini sui de. Cb

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">o. S.</hi> 325, <hi rend="italic">Sp.</hi> 2 <hi rend="italic">aus II Cn.</hi> 22, 2
notes.en: above p. 325, col. 2, from II Cn. 22, 2

passages.en: [61] <hi rend="bold">If</hi> moreover a free man of rank, that is a <hi rend="italic">þegen</hi> [thegn], <hi rend="spaced">had so advanced</hi> that he served the king and rode <hi rend="spaced">in his stead</hi> on the king's <hi rend="bold">mission</hi>, such a one, if he had <hi rend="spaced">another under him</hi> who held five hides for the king's <hi rend="bold">expedition</hi> and had served his lord in the king's hall and had three times gone to the king as his lord's messenger, such a one, <hi rend="spaced">I say</hi>, <hi rend="spaced">can</hi> thenceforth swear the fore-oath for his lord, <hi rend="bold">which we named above</hi> <hi rend="italic">foraþ</hi> [fore-oath], <hi rend="bold">in various matters,</hi> wherever there is need.

passages.text: [61, 1] Qui autem talem<ptr n="18" target="Gethyn_4.lnote.oe.18"/> non haberet, per semetipsum id <hi rend="spaced">faceret aut</hi> caréret.
passages.en: [61, 1] But whoever did not have such a one would <hi rend="spaced">do</hi> it by himself <hi rend="spaced">or</hi> go without.

passages.text: [61, 2] Et si liberalis homo ita<ptr n="1" target="Gethyn_5.lnote.oe.1"/> ascendisset, ut comes fieret, habebat<ptr n="2" target="Gethyn_5.lnote.oe.2"/> <hi rend="spaced">omnes rectitudines suas sicut</hi> comes.
passages.en: [61, 2] And if a free man of rank had so risen that he became an earl, he had <hi rend="spaced">all his rights as</hi> an earl.

passages.text: [62] Si mercator ter mare transisset suo proprio sumptu, talis deinde erat liberalitate<ptr n="3" target="Gethyn_6.lnote.oe.3"/> dignus, <hi rend="spaced">quod dicunt</hi> þegenrihtes<ptr n="4" target="Gethyn_6.lnote.oe.4"/> þurðe<ptr n="5" target="Gethyn_6.lnote.oe.5"/>.
passages.en: [62] If a merchant had three times crossed the sea at his own expense, such a one was thenceforth worthy of nobility, <hi rend="spaced">which they call</hi> <hi rend="italic">þegenrihtes þurðe</hi> [worthy of thegn-right].

passages.text: [63] Ita <hi rend="spaced">etiam</hi> et<ptr n="1" target="Gethyn_7.lnote.oe.1-2"/> clericus, qui discendo tantum profecerat, ut ordines haberet et <hi rend="bold">in castitate</hi><ptr n="a" target="Gethyn_7.lnote.oe.a"/> Christo seruiret, is<ptr n="6" target="Gethyn_7.lnote.oe.6"/> tunc iudicabatur <hi rend="spaced">iure in omnibus</hi> <hi rend="bold">liberalitatem</hi><ptr n="a" target="Gethyn_7.lnote.oe.a"/><ptr n="7" target="Gethyn_7.lnote.oe.7"/> habere debere.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">aus I Cn.</hi> 6, 2<hi rend="italic">a? Vgl. Inst. III</hi> 45 (Að 2, <hi rend="italic">S.</hi> 465, <hi rend="italic">Cölibat einschärfend</hi>)
notes.en: from I Cn. 6, 2a? Cf. Inst. III 45 (Að 2, p. 465, enjoining celibacy)

passages.en: [63] So <hi rend="spaced">also</hi> a cleric too, who by learning had advanced so far that he had orders and served Christ <hi rend="bold">in chastity</hi>, he was then judged <hi rend="spaced">by right in all things</hi> to be bound to have <hi rend="bold">nobility</hi>.

passages.text: [63, 1] Et si <hi rend="bold">contigerit</hi><ptr n="8" target="Gethyn_8.lnote.oe.8"/>, aliquem nocuisse ordinato<ptr n="9" target="Gethyn_8.lnote.oe.9"/> aut peregrino, tunc rex et episcopus <hi rend="spaced">iuste</hi>, quam citius possent<ptr n="10" target="Gethyn_8.lnote.oe.10"/>, hoc deberent<ptr n="11" target="Gethyn_8.lnote.oe.11"/> emendare<ptr n="12" target="Gethyn_8.lnote.oe.12"/>.
passages.en: [63, 1] And if it <hi rend="bold">should happen</hi> that someone has injured an ordained man or a stranger, then the king and the bishop ought <hi rend="spaced">justly</hi> to make amends for it as quickly as they could.

passages.text: <hi rend="small">Cornu bouis <hi rend="spaced">persoluitur</hi> decem denariis et uaccę duobus denariis;</hi>
passages.en: <hi rend="small">The horn of an ox <hi rend="spaced">is paid for</hi> with ten pence and of a cow with two pence;</hi>
